# Assistant fallback workflows

The native workflows for the current client are preferred. When a named skill is unavailable, use these complete contracts with discovered DCT tools and the local CLI where required. These are generated from the same authored sources as both clients' skills; do not maintain an independent behavior copy.

- **Language.** A quoted question, option, screen or report fixes what it
  says, not its wording: write it in the language of the conversation. Keep
  unchanged: identifiers, commands, paths, file contents, commit messages,
  changelog entries, short titles and anything shown verbatim.

The common consent boundary is the exact readable proposal before the user's explicit response. A selected default, timeout, silence, unattended run, old handoff or generated proposal is never approval. Changed scope requires a fresh concrete preview; reuse unchanged explicit consent already given. A report is not a consent request. Keep every proposal word visible before acceptance; hidden thinking, truncated content and a reference to an unavailable screen do not suffice.

Use the current host's eligible consent UI when it exposes complete previews; otherwise show the full decision material in visible text and ask for the explicit reply. Workflow references to dialog previews/Details pages mean the same complete readable content, translated to the current host's supported presentation. Never depend on hidden thinking, omitted pages or a Plan-only/optional-question-only permission tool.

Discover only tools needed by the selected branch, using the current host's available discovery mechanism. Invoke tools with separate top-level parameters from their actual descriptions; illustrative `mcp__dct__` prefixes name DCT tools, not a requirement for one host's namespace. An unavailable operation is a readable capability refusal, never a reason for direct SQL or ad hoc Python writes.

Use the available MCP discovery mechanism. No client-specific discovery tool, task mirror, hooks or publisher is assumed.

Use truthful actor identity in `created_by` and `consumed_by`. Only the true client is mandatory. Model, session identifier and session link are included only when supplied by the host; never invent them.

A project suffix is included only from a prior successful DCT response or an explicit user-supplied slug, never a directory, worktree or task-title guess. UTC is included only from an actual provided clock, known host time context or a time tool; no approximate time. Otherwise omit unknown components entirely, including project and time: never fill them with `unknown`, `?`, `0000` or guessed values. Server-created `created_at` / `consumed_at` timestamps remain separate ledger facts.

Use `<known_actor_identity>` in calls. A client-only identity such as `Codex` or `Claude Code` is sufficient when nothing else is known. Full-format example, ONLY when all components are known: `<true client>[-<host-supplied model>] @ <verified project slug> <actual UTC time>`. The same known-component rule applies to creation and consumption.

No mandatory extra lookup or preflight is added to AUTO pickup. Preserve its one-call path; do not obtain a slug by a guessed directory mapping, call a writer to bypass a read-only schema refusal, or require a clock lookup merely to fill an optional component. A status question remains a pure read with no `consumed_by` required.

Identify the actual assistant client. Capability and identity information must come from the running host.

When a shared read (`get_context_snapshot` or `pickup_work(consume="false")`, CLI `dct pickup --consume never`) refuses with SchemaNotReady, explain that setup or a schema upgrade is required. Propose `dct db upgrade` with explicit consent, then retry the original read only after that migration succeeds. Never invoke an unrelated writer to trigger a hidden migration. A SQLite reader may create WAL/SHM sidecars; it does not initialize the database, change journal mode, schema or data. Do not infer this guarantee for other list/get tools.

## Changelog proof: trailers and range (shared by `commit` and `release`)

A changelog entry is **proven** for a release when a commit in the release
range names its id in a `Changelog:` trailer. `commit` writes the trailers,
the release workflow reads them. The rules are implemented ONCE in code —
`dct/workflows/release/proof.py` (trailers, reverts, squash signals) and
`dct/workflows/release/plan.py` (range, provenance, candidates) — and
computed read-only by two commands whose JSON schemas, range rule (K-71),
revert rule (K-68), squash heuristic and its limits (K-69) and provenance
(K-70) are documented in [release-workflow.md](release-workflow.md):

- `dct release plan [-P slug] [--version V | --patch|--minor|--major]
  [--entries <ids> | --no-entries] --json` — the release plan of the
  current checkout; on the CLI path its `snapshot` / `snapshot_digest` is
  what the owner approves (K-80) — `release` reads it for routing and
  approves the preview's screen instead. No side effects.
- `dct clog candidates [-P slug] --json` — `commit`'s candidates:
  `confirmed` vs `uncertain`, minus the ids the range already proves, plus
  the staged file list.

The essentials an assistant must know to write and read proof (the code is
authoritative):

- **Trailer format** (written by `commit`): one line `Changelog: <id>, <id>`
  — ids ascending, comma + space — in the final trailer block, before
  `Co-Authored-By:`. Release commits (`release: vX.Y.Z`) carry none.
- **What counts** (per commit of the range): git's trailer parser
  (`%(trailers:key=Changelog,valueonly,separator=%x2C)`) plus every body line
  matching `^Changelog: [0-9]+(, [0-9]+)*$` in column 0. The strict format is
  RESERVED (K-66): a column-0 line in an example counts too, so quote or
  indent examples; quoted, bulleted and indented lines never count.
- **Range**: from the nearest release tag that is an ancestor of the
  candidate; the plan flags `confirm_required` when that is not the tag of
  `current_version` (show it, the owner confirms) and `approximate` when no
  ancestor tag exists (warn).
- **Reverts**: `commit` writes reverts with git's standard message
  (`Revert "<subject>"` + `This reverts commit <sha>.`) — that is what the
  workflow detects; the reverted commit's ids lose their proof.
- **Squash merges lose trailers**: a title-only squash drops the bodies, a
  local `git merge --squash` indents them. The plan proposes ONE collective
  attestation per source branch (`attestation_groups`) — a proposal the
  owner confirms, never an automatic assignment. Recommended merge modes:
  [release-workflow.md](release-workflow.md#merge-policy).
- **Uncertain entries** (`branch_source='server'` — the MCP server's own
  checkout — or no provenance) and every entry on a **detached HEAD** are
  never attached as found: match them against the staged diff, ask, and
  confirm them with `update_changelog(entry_id, branch=<current>,
  worktree=<toplevel>)` (detached: `worktree` only) first. Never fall into an
  unfiltered list of every branch. The commit hook's count is only a gate
  (are there entries at all?), never proof that an entry belongs to the
  commit — the trailer set is always chosen from the final staged diff.
- **Attestation** — the only way to add proof after the fact — is the empty
  commit `chore: attest changelog entries` created by `dct release attest
  --entries <ids> --confirm` once the owner confirms the changes are in the
  candidate (in `release`: the owner's "Release with all N" or "Change
  something" answer, and `apply --consent` makes the same commit).

## `/clog` fallback

### clog — Add Changelog Entry

#### Workflow

##### Step 1: Gather from context
From the current work, determine:
- **project**: Auto-detect from CWD; ask only when the project is ambiguous
  (CWD not registered)
- **category**: added, changed, fixed, removed (see mapping below); ask only
  when the category is genuinely ambiguous
- **entry**: Concise description of the change (English, ~1 sentence)
- **component**: Module/subsystem (optional)
- **source_file**: Main file changed (optional)
- **source_lines**: Line range in that file, e.g. "42-58" (optional)
- **related_item_id**: If this change resolves a tracked item (optional)
- **branch** / **worktree**: Read in YOUR current working directory:
  `git branch --show-current` (empty output = detached HEAD → omit `branch`)
  and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`. Always pass them — the MCP server
  runs in the session start directory, which may be another checkout or
  worktree, so its own guess can name the wrong branch.

##### Step 2: Write — no confirmation question
An unambiguous instruction ("clog this", "log the parser fix", right after a
finished change) writes the entry without a confirmation question: call
`mcp__dct__add_changelog(project, category, entry, branch, worktree, ...)` at
once. An entry is cheap to correct, so the acknowledgement (Step 3) is the
check.

The ack echoes `branch` and `branch_source`; if `branch` is missing from the
ack, the MCP server is older than this skill — tell the user to restart it.
If the ack says `branch_source: "server"` (it then carries a `warning`), the
server filled in ITS OWN checkout, not yours — the entry is NOT confirmed.
Correct it right away against your actual checkout:
`mcp__dct__update_changelog(id, branch=<yours>, worktree=<yours>)` (both
fields; on a detached HEAD pass only `worktree`). `commit` never attaches a
server-detected entry without that correction.

##### Step 3: Acknowledge in one line
```
✓ Changelog #15 [added] — New Python parser support (feat/x) · to change it: "#15: <new text>" · to remove it: "delete #15"
```
One line per entry: id, category, text, branch — and it ENDS with how to
correct it, in words the user can type back; never left out, the write had
no question. "#15: <new text>" → `mcp__dct__update_changelog(15, entry=…)`
(any other field likewise); "delete #15" withdraws an entry that should not
exist with `mcp__dct__delete_changelog(15)`.

#### Category mapping
| Change type | category |
|---|---|
| New feature, new file, new capability | added |
| Refactor, rename, restructure, update behavior | changed |
| Bug fix, crash fix, correction | fixed |
| Deleted code, removed feature, deprecated | removed |

#### Conventional commit → category
| Prefix | category |
|---|---|
| feat: | added |
| fix: | fixed |
| refactor:, chore:, perf: | changed |
| revert: | removed |

#### Multiple entries

If a commit touches multiple areas, create multiple changelog entries —
one per logical change. Example: refactor that also fixes a bug and adds
a helper:

```
✓ Changelog #20 [changed] — Extracted shared auth validation (core/auth)
✓ Changelog #21 [fixed]   — Token refresh race condition on concurrent login (core/auth)
✓ Changelog #22 [added]   — is_expired() helper on Session model (core/auth)
  to change one: "#21: <new text>" · to remove one: "delete #21"
```

Each entry is a separate `add_changelog` call. Don't concatenate changes
into one entry — it makes the generated changelog.md harder to skim at
release time.

  unchanged: identifiers, commands, paths, file contents, commit messages,
  changelog entries, short titles and anything shown verbatim.

A selected default, timeout, silence, unattended run, old handoff or generated proposal is never approval. Changed scope requires a fresh concrete preview; reuse unchanged explicit consent already given. A report is not a consent request. Keep every proposal word visible before acceptance; hidden thinking, truncated content and a reference to an unavailable screen do not suffice.

Use the current host's eligible consent UI when it exposes complete previews; otherwise show the full decision material in visible text and ask for the explicit reply. Workflow references to dialog previews/Details pages mean the same complete readable content, translated to the current host's supported presentation. Never depend on hidden thinking, omitted pages or a Plan-only/optional-question-only permission tool.


Discover only tools needed by the selected branch, using the current host's available discovery mechanism. Invoke tools with separate top-level parameters from their actual descriptions; illustrative `mcp__dct__` prefixes name DCT tools, not a requirement for one host's namespace. ## `/commit` fallback

### commit — Git Commit (dct-aware)

Universal commit workflow. Auto-detects the project from CWD and mirrors the
global hook's exemption rules so the first attempt passes. The owner sees ONE
screen — the files, the message and the entries the commit marks as done —
and answers it once (Step 6).

#### Tool discovery

Discover only tools needed by the selected branch, using the current host's available discovery mechanism. Invoke tools with separate top-level parameters from their actual descriptions; illustrative `mcp__dct__` prefixes name DCT tools, not a requirement for one host's namespace. An unavailable operation is a readable capability refusal, never a reason for direct SQL or ad hoc Python writes.

Use the available MCP discovery mechanism. No client-specific discovery tool, task mirror, hooks or publisher is assumed.

Load `list_projects`, `count_unreleased_changelog`, `list_changelog` and `update_changelog` before preflight when deferred.

The trailer format and the range / proof rules are implemented ONCE by the
release workflow (`dct clog candidates --json`, `dct release plan --json`;
schemas in `docs/release-workflow.md`) and described in
`docs/assistant-fallbacks.md` ("Changelog proof: trailers and range") — on
divergence the code and that doc win.

#### Workflow

##### Step 1: Preflight (ONE parallel message)

Run all probes in a single parallel message:
- `git status`
- `git diff --cached --stat`
- `git diff --stat`
- `git log --oneline -5`
- `git branch --show-current` (empty = detached HEAD) and `git rev-parse --show-toplevel`
- `mcp__dct__list_projects()` — match longest path prefix → `slug`, `current_version`
  and the stored trailer preferences `commit_co_authored_by` /
  `commit_session_link` (no row = not a dct project)
- `dct clog candidates --json` (dct project only) — its `secret_like` list
  names the changed files whose path looks like a secret (Step 4); the
  trailer candidates are read again in Step 5, after the staging
- `mcp__dct__count_unreleased_changelog(project, branch=<current>, include_unbranched=true)`
  — changelog count for this branch (uncertain entries — no branch, or
  server-detected — count too); detached HEAD → omit `branch`
  (project-wide count — a gate only, never a candidate list)

If nothing changed AND nothing staged → "Clean tree, nothing to commit", stop.
New (untracked) files are changes like any other: Step 4 applies the same
rules to them — no question of their own (a commit of new files only, such
as a new module or a first commit, gets the one screen too).

##### Step 2: Version-bump redirect to release

If staged changes look like a version bump, STOP and suggest `release`:
- `changelog.md` / `CHANGELOG.md` staged AND contains a new `## [X.Y.Z]` heading
- A staged `version = "..."` change in `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `tauri.conf.json`, `plugin.json`

Only a STAGED version bump redirects here. The number of unreleased entries
is never a reason to suggest `release` — when to release is the owner's
call.

Ask via the supported decision interaction: "Staged changes look like a version bump. Prefer release?"
→ `"Run release instead"` / `"No — regular commit"` / `"Cancel"`. Release commits
use the literal `release: vX.Y.Z` format (no scope, no version suffix).

##### Step 3: Changelog guard

If a project was detected and `count == 0` (per branch, see Step 1) AND the
files to commit contain non-exempt code, ask via the supported decision interaction: "No unreleased changelog entry. Add one now?"
→ "Yes, via clog" (invoke `clog` or `add_changelog` inline) / "Skip (warn: may
hit the hook)" / "Cancel".

The count is ONLY this gate (are there entries at all?) — never proof that an
entry belongs to this commit. Which entries the commit carries is decided in
Step 5, from the final staged diff.

**Exempt patterns** (no changelog required if ALL staged files match). They
decide only whether an entry is REQUIRED — attaching an existing matching entry
(Step 5) is always allowed, exempt paths or not:
- `.claude/`, `.claude-plugin/`, `.github/`, `.cursor/`, `.vscode/`, `.gstack/`
- `docs/`, `scripts/`, `tests/`, `dct/skills/`, `test_*.py`, `conftest.py`
- `CLAUDE.md`, `CLAUDE.local.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `LICENSE*`
- `changelog.md`, `CHANGELOG*`, `.gitignore`
- Config files: `pyproject.toml`, `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `biome.json`, `tsconfig*.json`

**Paths that look like a secret** — ONE predicate, shared with `release`:
the `secret_like` list of `dct clog candidates --json` (`{path, staged,
unstage}` for every changed file — staged, unstaged and untracked). It judges
a path by its file name only and is never a content scanner: `.env`,
`.env.*`, `*.pem`, `*.key`, `id_rsa*`, `*.p12`, `credentials*.json`; the
templates `*.example` / `*.sample` (`.env.example`, `.env.sample`) are
ordinary files, like any other configuration. Without the CLI (not a dct
project, CLI missing) apply exactly these name patterns by hand.

**Blacklist — NEVER stage:** every secret-like path above, binaries,
generated artifacts (`dist/`, `build/`, `target/`, `*.pyc`).

##### Step 4: Stage (explicit paths) — BEFORE selecting the trailer

The order is fixed: **stage (Step 4) → select (Step 5) → commit (Step 6)**.
The trailer attests what the commit CONTAINS, so the index must hold exactly
the commit's content before any entry is chosen, and nothing is staged after
the choice.

Stage path by path — never `git add -A`, `git add .`, or globs:

```bash
git add -- dct/core/items.py tests/test_items.py
```

- A path that is ALREADY partially staged (it shows in both
  `git diff --cached` and `git diff`) is a deliberate choice: leave it as it
  is — never re-add the whole file unless the user asks to include its
  unstaged hunks too.
- When the user staged everything themselves, there is nothing to add — the
  index is the plan (but see the secret-like stop below).
- A secret-like path that is unstaged or untracked is never offered for
  staging and never staged: it stays out, and the Step 6 screen names it
  under "Not included (looks like a secret)".
- **A secret-like path that is already staged STOPS the commit** before the
  screen. Say it in one plain sentence — "`.env` is staged and looks like a
  secret, so I stop here" — and show its `unstage` command exactly as the
  candidates give it (quoted, with the `--` separator: `git restore --staged
  -- .env`; before the first commit `git rm --cached -q -- .env`). Never run
  that command yourself and never change the user's index — the user decides.
  If the file really belongs in the repository, the user commits it with git
  directly; `commit` never does.

Stage without a question when the choice is clear: the changed files are the
work the entries describe. Ask via the supported decision interaction only when there is a real
choice — several changed files that do not all belong to the entries (which of
them go into this commit?). A blacklisted path (secret-like, a binary, a
generated artifact) is never an option of that question: it stays out and the
screen lists it. The files staged here are shown on the Step 6 screen, where
"Change" can still alter them.

##### Step 5: Select the `Changelog:` trailer from the FINAL staged diff

The trailer is the proof the release workflow reads later: an entry no
commit names is released only after an explicit attestation. The rules are
computed by the workflow, not by this skill (`dct/workflows/release/`,
schema `docs/release-workflow.md`):

1. **Candidates** — Step 4 is done, the index is final. Run
   `dct clog candidates --json` in the current checkout. It returns
   `confirmed` (client-recorded entries of THIS branch and checkout),
   `uncertain` (server-detected or without provenance, whatever branch they
   store; on a detached HEAD every entry of this checkout), `other_branch`,
   `already_proven` (ids a commit of the range already names — never cited
   again) and `staged_files`. Show its `warnings` (detached HEAD, approximate
   range). **CLI missing or too old:** retrieve the unreleased rows with
   `mcp__dct__list_changelog(project=<selected slug>, unreleased_only=true)`
   and classify them by hand against the current branch and actual toplevel.
   `branch_source="client"` plus this branch AND checkout is confirmed;
   server-detected or absent provenance is uncertain regardless of its stored
   branch/worktree. A client row of this branch with no worktree is uncertain;
   client rows proven to belong to another checkout are excluded. On detached
   HEAD no row is confirmed: this checkout's candidates remain uncertain.
   Client rows from another branch remain `other_branch`, never a confirmed
   list of every branch. Exclude `already_proven` ids under the same release
   range, trailer, revert and squash rules described above; disclose an
   approximate or unverifiable range, never treat the raw list as proof.
   Then apply Steps 2–5 below: compare the complete staged diff and obtain
   consent before confirming an uncertain row against the actual checkout.
2. **Match against the complete `git diff --cached`** (and `staged_files`):
   keep the `confirmed` candidates whose entry text / `source_file` describe
   what is staged. Ask via the supported decision interaction when unsure.
3. **`uncertain` candidates are matched too, but never attached
   automatically.** When one matches the staged diff, ask; only on
   "yes" confirm it against the ACTUAL checkout first —
   `mcp__dct__update_changelog(entry_id, branch=<current>, worktree=<toplevel>)`
   (both fields) — then attach it. A candidate that describes another change
   is left alone.
4. **Detached HEAD** (`checkout.detached`): a soft presence check only.
   There are no confirmed candidates; every entry of this checkout is
   `uncertain` (`detached_head`) — ask which (if any) the commit carries.
   Confirm a server-detected one with
   `mcp__dct__update_changelog(entry_id, worktree=<toplevel>)` (no branch
   exists; its unconfirmed branch is cleared). Never fall back to an
   unfiltered list of every branch.
5. **No match, but `other_branch` entries describe the staged change**
   (recorded before a branch rename or switch) → offer
   `mcp__dct__update_changelog(entry_id, branch=<current>)`, then re-select.
6. Format: ONE line `Changelog: <id>, <id>` — ids ascending, comma + space —
   in the final trailer block, before `Co-Authored-By:`. No selected ids → no
   `Changelog:` line.
7. **The strict format is reserved**: a column-0 line
   `Changelog: <ids>` ANYWHERE in the message counts as proof. When a body
   shows the format as an example, quote or indent it (`> Changelog: 12`) so
   it proves nothing.

##### Step 6: Commit — one screen, then `git commit` WITHOUT another `git add`

The screen — the staged files, the full message and the entries the trailer
marks as done — travels inside the dialog, as the preview of the "Commit"
option (Rules: "The screen travels inside the dialog"):

```
Commit on feat/x — 2 files
  dct/core/items.py
  tests/test_items.py
Message:
  feat(core): add checkpoint CRUD (v0.1.0)

  Changelog: 12, 15
  Co-Authored-By: <actual assistant co-author identity supplied by host>
Entries marked as done: #12 [added] Checkpoint CRUD · #15 [fixed] Empty title crash
```

ONE decision interaction — "Commit 2 files on feat/x?" → "Commit" (its preview:
the screen) / "Change — I will say what" / "Stop". A screen longer than 15
lines (many files, a long body) continues on the "Details" pages of the same
dialog. NEVER commit without the owner's "Commit" on this screen.

- **"Commit"** → run the commit below, exactly what Step 4 staged.
- **"Change"** → apply what the owner says. A change of the message only
  (wording, type, scope, a trailer dropped or added for this one commit) is
  applied and the dialog is asked again with the new screen. A change that
  touches the files (add or drop a path, re-stage) changes the index, so the
  selection is stale: stage it by the Step 4 rules, redo Step 5 against the
  new `git diff --cached`, then ask the dialog again with the new screen.
- **"Stop"** → nothing is committed; the index stays as it is.

**Trailers** follow the project's stored preferences from the Step 1
`list_projects` row, applied without a question:

- `commit_co_authored_by` true → a `Co-Authored-By:` trailer (the actual host-supplied identity); false → none.
- `commit_session_link` true → the session link the client gives for this
  session (only its real host-supplied link); false → none. A session
  link is written only on a stored true (yes).
- null = not answered yet (never a "no"): ask ONCE — one decision interaction
  before the screen, both preferences in it — store the answers with
  `dct project trailers <slug> --co-authored-by on|off --session-link on|off`
  and apply them; the question never comes again for that project.

The project's own rules win: read them from the project's instruction
  files on disk at the repository top level — `AGENTS.md` and, where the
  project still keeps rules there, `CLAUDE.md` / `CLAUDE.local.md` (also
  `.claude/CLAUDE.md`); a project with only `AGENTS.md` is read the same
  way. Never rely on the client's automatic `@import` expansion: a line
  `@<path>` in one of them means: read `<path>` yourself. When the project's
  own rules in any of them forbid a trailer, it is never written whatever
  is stored, never offered as an option to approve again, and stored as
  `off` when the preferences are asked. dct's own repository forbids a
  session link (OSS hygiene, in its `AGENTS.md`).
- Not a dct project (no row): nothing can be stored — `Co-Authored-By` by
  default, never a session link.

Use truthful actor identity in `created_by` and `consumed_by`. Only the true client is mandatory. Model, session identifier and session link are included only when supplied by the host; never invent them.

A project suffix is included only from a prior successful DCT response or an explicit user-supplied slug, never a directory, worktree or task-title guess. UTC is included only from an actual provided clock, known host time context or a time tool; no approximate time. Otherwise omit unknown components entirely, including project and time: never fill them with `unknown`, `?`, `0000` or guessed values. Server-created `created_at` / `consumed_at` timestamps remain separate ledger facts.

Use `<known_actor_identity>` in calls. A client-only identity such as `Codex` or `Claude Code` is sufficient when nothing else is known. Full-format example, ONLY when all components are known: `<true client>[-<host-supplied model>] @ <verified project slug> <actual UTC time>`. The same known-component rule applies to creation and consumption.

No mandatory extra lookup or preflight is added to AUTO pickup. Preserve its one-call path; do not obtain a slug by a guessed directory mapping, call a writer to bypass a read-only schema refusal, or require a clock lookup merely to fill an optional component. A status question remains a pure read with no `consumed_by` required.

Identify the actual assistant client. Capability and identity information must come from the running host.

"Change" can drop or add a trailer for this one commit; the stored preference
changes only through `dct project trailers`.

```bash
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
<type>(<scope>): <description> (v<current_version>)

Optional body paragraph explaining WHY (not what).

Changelog: 12, 15
Co-Authored-By: <actual assistant co-author identity supplied by host>
EOF
)"
```

- No `git add` here and no `git commit -a` / `git commit <paths>` — any of
  them would change the content after the trailer was chosen.
- `type` ∈ {feat, fix, refactor, chore, docs, test, perf, style, revert};
  `scope` = component (`core`, `cli`, `server`, …);
  `description` = imperative, lowercase, no trailing period, ≤ 72 chars.
- `(v<version>)` suffix — OMIT if `current_version` is null or this IS the release commit.
- Release commits use the literal `release: vX.Y.Z` format instead, and carry
  NO `Changelog:` trailer.
- **Reverts** keep git's standard message so the release workflow
  sees the revert: `git revert --no-commit <sha>` stages it (Step 4), then
  the subject is exactly `Revert "<original subject>"` and the body holds the
  column-0 line `This reverts commit <full sha>.` (git's own wording; no
  conventional type, no version suffix). The entries the reverted commit
  proved lose that proof — never cite them in the revert's trailer.
- The `Changelog:` line is the Step 5 selection; omit it when nothing was selected.

##### Step 7: Hook-reject recovery

If a hook rejects the commit:
1. Read the error — it says exactly what's missing.
2. Fix the underlying issue (usually: add a changelog entry via `clog`).
3. Stage the files of the fix explicitly (Step 4 rules).
4. ANY change to the index — re-staging, a new file — makes the selection
   stale: redo Step 5 against the new `git diff --cached` (a new `clog`
   entry is now a candidate).
5. Create a **NEW** commit (Step 6) — never `--amend` (the rejected commit never happened).
6. Never bypass with `--no-verify`, `--no-gpg-sign`, or similar.

##### Step 8: Verify (ONE command)

```bash
git log --oneline -3 && git status
```

Report: `✓ Committed abc1234 — feat(core): add checkpoint CRUD (v0.1.0) · Changelog: 12, 15`
(or `· no Changelog trailer`).

#### Rules (hard)

- **Language.** A quoted question, option, screen or report fixes what it
  says, not its wording: write it in the language of the conversation. Keep
  unchanged: identifiers, commands, paths, file contents, commit messages,
  changelog entries, short titles and anything shown verbatim.
The common consent boundary is the exact readable proposal before the user's explicit response. A selected default, timeout, silence, unattended run, old handoff or generated proposal is never approval. Changed scope requires a fresh concrete preview; reuse unchanged explicit consent already given. A report is not a consent request. Keep every proposal word visible before acceptance; hidden thinking, truncated content and a reference to an unavailable screen do not suffice.

Use the current host's eligible consent UI when it exposes complete previews; otherwise show the full decision material in visible text and ask for the explicit reply. Workflow references to dialog previews/Details pages mean the same complete readable content, translated to the current host's supported presentation. Never depend on hidden thinking, omitted pages or a Plan-only/optional-question-only permission tool.
- NEVER commit without the owner's "Commit" on the Step 6 screen (files,
  message, entries); "Stop" commits nothing.
- NEVER select the `Changelog:` trailer before the staging is final, and NEVER
  stage anything after selecting it (Step 4 → Step 5 → Step 6).
- NEVER replace a deliberate partial staging with the whole file.
- NEVER stage `.env`, any other secret-like path (`secret_like`), binaries, or
  anything matching the blacklist; a staged secret-like path stops the commit
  with its quoted `unstage` command, and the index stays as the user left it.
- NEVER use `git add -A`, `git add .`, or broad globs.
- NEVER use `--amend` unless the user explicitly asks (to edit a successful commit).
- NEVER use `--no-verify`. Hooks exist for reasons — if blocked, fix and re-commit.
- NEVER force-push to main/master branches.
- Trailers follow the project's stored preferences without a question (one
  question, once, while they are not answered yet); the project's own rules
  forbidding a trailer win — never a session link in dct's own repository.
- Release commits use literal `release: vX.Y.Z` format — no scope, no description,
  no `Changelog:` trailer.
- NEVER attach an `uncertain` candidate (null `branch`, `branch_source='server'`,
  detached HEAD) without asking and confirming it via `update_changelog`.
- Reverts keep git's standard `Revert "…"` / `This reverts commit <sha>.`
  message; examples of the trailer format in a body are quoted.

## `/dct-import` fallback

### dct-import — Import Existing Tracking Data

#### Two import paths (v0.2.0)

Markdown files fall into three buckets; each uses a different tool:

| Bucket       | Files                                                       | Tool                                     |
| ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| **Plan-like**| plans, specs, ADRs, roadmaps, retros, backlogs              | `mcp__dct__ingest_plan_file` (v0.2 pipeline) |
| **Issue-like**| ORCH-N / BUG-N custom-field files, TODOS with inline status | v0.1 items + checkpoints (see Pattern Catalog below) |
| **Changelog**| CHANGELOG.md, changelog.md, changelog_unreleased.md         | `add_changelog` for unreleased; `import_released_changelog` for history |

The v0.2 pipeline handles ULID injection, `[x]` historical state, and
optional LLM classification of uncertain sections in one call — you don't
re-implement Pattern Catalog logic for plan-like files.

#### Key principle

The assistant proposes; the user decides through the supported decision interaction. Never auto-create
without confirmation. Ambiguous entries are flagged and asked one-by-one.

#### Workflow

##### Step 1: Detect candidate files

Scan project root (and common subdirs) for typical tracking files. Apply
the stale-file skip list FIRST (see below) — do not even offer skipped
paths to the user.

Typical patterns (file name heuristic):
- **Plan-like** (→ `ingest_plan_file`):
  - `docs/plans/*.md`, `docs/specs/*.md`, `docs/adr/*.md`, `docs/retros/*.md`
  - `ROADMAP.md`, `TODOS.md`, `FUTURE.md`, `BACKLOG.md`
  - `SPRINT*.md`, `PLAN*.md`
- **Issue-like** (→ v0.1 items path):
  - `ISSUES.md`, `BUGS.md`, `*issues*.md`, `*orchestrator*.md`
- **Changelog** (→ `add_changelog`):
  - `CHANGELOG.md`, `changelog.md`, `changelog_unreleased.md`

##### Step 2: Classify each file by format

For each candidate, read the first ~60 lines and classify by content.
The Pattern Catalog below lists 10 known formats. A file may match multiple
(e.g. a plan with embedded checkboxes) — pick the dominant one, flag as
composite in Step 4.

##### Step 3: Parse per-format

Apply the mapping rules from the Pattern Catalog. Build a draft table of
proposed imports BEFORE any DB write.

##### Step 4: Present review — decision interaction pipeline

First decision interaction:
- question: "Found N files. Which to import?"
- options: one per file formatted `TODOS.md (304 lines) — checkbox TODOs`,
  plus `"All detected files"`, `"Pick subset (I'll list)"`, `"Cancel"`.
- On subset: follow-up multi-select decision interaction.

For each selected file, ONE decision interaction with the proposed table inside
it — the preview of "Import all as listed", on "Details" pages when longer
than 15 lines (Rules: "The screen travels inside the dialog"):
- question: "Proceed with <file>? (N entries, M ambiguous)"
- options:
  - `"Import all as listed"`
  - `"Resolve ambiguities one-by-one"` — one decision interaction per flagged row
  - `"Edit first"` — free-text decision interaction, parse corrections, ask
    again with the corrected table
  - `"Skip this file"`
  - `"Cancel import"`

##### Step 5: Execute

Check existing items/history before importing to avoid a known duplicate. Imports are per operation, not a whole-file transaction; retain every acknowledged id and report partial completion. After an ambiguous write response inspect its result before retrying.

**For plan-like files** (v0.2 pipeline):
- Pass a real boolean: call `mcp__dct__ingest_plan_file(file_path, project, auto_resolve_uncertain=true)` only when the owner approved using the configured `rules` or `command` strategy for that import. For skipping resolution, an unapproved strategy, or a disabled/unavailable provider, call `mcp__dct__ingest_plan_file(file_path, project, auto_resolve_uncertain=false)`. Never pass a strategy name or prose as the boolean. Respect the configuration; do not force a Claude invocation. Show the configured command/provider and unknown cost where applicable before strategy consent.
- The tool handles ULID injection, DB upsert, first-import `[x]` historical
  state, and optional LLM classification in one call.
- This DOES modify the MD file by injecting `<!-- dct:plan/section/cp:<ULID> -->`
  HTML comments — this is intentional; the anchors are the stable cross-cut
  between file and DB. Original text / ordering / code blocks are preserved.

For each confirmed issue-like or changelog entry (legacy v0.1 path):
1. Items: `mcp__dct__create_item(...)` — **REMEMBER the returned `id`** per entry.
   Pass a `short_title` for every item: a 2-4 word English noun phrase naming
   what it is about (≤ 50 chars, no item number, no project name), derived
   from the title — even when the title itself stays in its source language.
   Every create ack must echo `short_title` (null when none was stored). A
   missing key means the MCP server's contract is outdated: STOP the import
   and report an unsupported server contract (restart / upgrade the server).
   Do NOT retry the create — that item already exists.
2. Parent + sub-tasks: after creating the parent item, loop
   `mcp__dct__add_checkpoint(parent_id, text)` for each sub-task —
   remember each checkpoint id. Mark already-done sub-tasks via
   `complete_checkpoint(cp_id)` in a second pass.
3. Changelog entries: `mcp__dct__add_changelog(...)`.
4. Provenance: `mcp__dct__add_note(item_id, f"Imported from {filename} on {date}")`
   for every item. This feeds the post-migration audit trail.
5. For issue-like / changelog: NEVER modify or delete the source markdown file.

##### Step 6: Report

Per-file summary: counts by type / priority / done-vs-open. End with
"X items, Y checkpoints, Z changelog entries imported from N files".

---

#### Pattern Catalog

##### Format A — TODOS.md (checkbox flat list)

```markdown
## P1 — Blockers
- [ ] Fix parser crash on empty files
- [x] Rotate session tokens  ← already done

## P2 — Important
- [ ] Add progress bar
```

Mapping:
- Section heading `## P1 — ...` → `priority="P1"` for items in that section
- `- [ ]` / `- [x]` → `status="open"` / `status="resolved"`
- `✅` or bare `**DONE**` or `STATUS: DONE` at entry end → equivalent to `[x]`
- Line after dash → `title` (strip bold markers, emoji, leading/trailing whitespace)
- `item_type` defaults to `todo` unless entry text matches type triggers
  ("bug", "crash", "error" → issue; "add X" → feature; etc.)

##### Format B — Narrative sprint / ROADMAP

```markdown
## Sprint 3 — January push

Goal: ship the parser rewrite, close the 4 blocker bugs, validate perf.

- Parser rewrite from scratch (new AST, incremental indexing)
- Memory leak fix in watcher — blocking prod since Jan 4
- Cross-platform CI matrix
- Performance baseline vs v0.17
```

Mapping (**plan-as-parent** strategy):
- Each `## Sprint N — <title>` or `## Sprint 0.5 — <title>` → ONE parent item:
  `item_type="feature"`, `title="Sprint N — <title>"`, description includes the Goal line
- Each bullet under the sprint → `add_checkpoint(parent_id, bullet_text)`
- Completed sprint (all bullets done, or marked "Done"/"✅ Shipped"):
  resolve parent + complete all checkpoints
- Recognize multilingual section markers: `## Sprint`, `## Iteration`,
  `## Faza`, `## Etap`

##### Format C — Custom issue format (ORCH-N, BUG-N)

```markdown
## ORCH-3 — Scheduler race on concurrent writes

**Where**: cmd/scheduler/dispatch.go:142
**Problem**: Two workers claim the same job when heartbeat skipped.
**Fix**: Add advisory lock around SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED.
**Severity**: P1
**Status**: open
```

Mapping:
- Heading → `title` (strip the ID prefix or capture it as tag — see the tag note below)
- `**Where**:` → `source_file` (+ `source_lines` if line range present)
- `**Problem**:` + `**Fix**:` → merged into `description`
- `**Severity**:` → `priority` (P1/P2/P3)
- `**Status**:` → `status` (map "open"/"in progress"/"done"/"resolved")
- `item_type="issue"` (that's what this format represents)
- Prefix like `ORCH-3` → `tags=["orch"]` (derive bucket tag from prefix)

**Tag note**: tags come from a global, normalized dictionary. A derived bucket
tag can trip the similarity guard against a name that already exists (`orch` vs
`orchestrator`) — the create is then REFUSED with a suggestion and the item is
rolled back. Default to the suggested existing tag; when the new bucket is
genuinely wanted, call `mcp__dct__add_tag(name=..., force=true)` once, then
re-run the import batch.

##### Format D — Plan-as-parent (1.5k+ line planning doc)

Large planning documents (1.5k-2k+ lines) SHOULD NOT be flattened into
hundreds of items. Instead:

1. File → ONE parent item: `item_type="feature"`, title from file H1,
   description = first prose section + link to file path.
2. Each `##` section → `add_checkpoint(parent_id, section_title)`.
3. Each checkbox WITHIN those sections → one more `add_checkpoint` (nested
   via sort_order grouping, e.g. section 1 gets sort 10-19, section 2 gets 20-29).
4. If file has >7 `##` sections, ask user via the supported decision interaction whether
   they prefer "one parent per section" (multiple items) instead.

##### Format E — Keep-a-Changelog with [Unreleased]

Standard format:
```markdown
## [Unreleased]
### Added
- New Python parser support

### Fixed
- Memory leak in watcher
```

Mapping:
- `### Added/Changed/Fixed/Removed` → `category` directly
- Bullet → `entry`
- Only import `[Unreleased]` section by default (past versions already released)

##### Format F — Keep-a-Changelog WITHOUT [Unreleased]

Some projects have only historical version sections. Ask whether to import the latest version as explicitly unreleased, import the exact historical rows with their stated versions/dates, or skip. A latest-as-unreleased choice uses `add_changelog` and is explicitly shown as such; it is not a discovered historical release.

Before historical writes, read existing history (`list_changelog(project=<slug>, unreleased_only=false)`) and preview exact category, entry, version, stated date (or import-time default), component/source and supported related item per row. Check duplicates against existing rows; this does not establish automatic deduplication or whole-file atomicity. Import only the approved files and rows.

Historical rows use `import_released_changelog(project=<slug>, category=<category>, entry=<text>, version=<original spelling>, released_at=<stated ISO-8601 or "">, component="", source_file="", source_lines="", related_item_id=0)`. Every field is a separate top-level parameter. CLI equivalent: `dct clog import-released <project> <category> <entry> --version <version> [--released-at <ISO-8601>] [--component ...] [--source-file ...] [--source-lines ...] [--related-item N] --json`.

A stated date-only value becomes 00:00:00 UTC on that day; full timestamps require an offset and normalize to UTC. Malformed timestamps write nothing for that row. An absent date uses current import time, reported as `released_at_source="import_time"`, never as a discovered original release date; supplied dates return `released_at_source="stated"`. The ack carries saved id/project/category/version/released_at/source; retain every returned id. Original version spelling is preserved. Versions with release records or above current_version refuse.

Per-row failure leaves earlier successful rows intact: report exact acknowledged ids, failed/unattempted rows and cause. An ambiguous response is inspected before any retry, never blindly imported again. No automatic branch/worktree attribution is made for historical events. Historical import changes neither current_version, unrelated unreleased entries nor release records. Never use add→release stamping, `release_changelog`, advance, tags, commits, reconstruction or compensating deletion for import. Preserve source Markdown for changelog/issue rows.

##### Format G — Empty subsections

```markdown
## [Unreleased]
### Added

### Fixed
- Actually something here
```

Skip empty subsections gracefully — do not create placeholder items. If
ALL subsections under [Unreleased] are empty, treat the file as "no
unreleased content" and move on.

##### Format H — FUTURE.md / IDEAS.md (prose or loose bullets)

```markdown
## Maybe someday

Would be cool to support Ruby parsers. The challenge is...

Another idea: plugin system for custom languages.
```

Mapping:
- Each H2/bullet → `item_type="idea"`, `priority="future"`
- Description = the prose underneath (first 500 chars)

##### Format I — Conventional-commit style entries

```markdown
- feat(parser): add Python support
- fix(watcher): memory leak on large trees
- refactor(graph): extract schema builder
```

Mapping (useful when importing from git log turned into markdown):
- Prefix `feat:` / `feat(scope):` → `category="added"`, `component=<scope>`
- `fix:` → `category="fixed"`
- `refactor:` / `chore:` / `perf:` / `style:` → `category="changed"`
- `revert:` / `remove:` → `category="removed"`
- Text after `:` → `entry`

##### Format J — No-changelog graceful case

If the project has NO changelog file, do NOT error. Report: `"No changelog
file found — skipping changelog import"` and continue with items only.

---

#### Stale-file skip list

Skip these paths during Step 1 detection — do NOT offer them to the user.
Common sources of already-migrated / archival / generated content:

- `.cursor/plans/`, `.cursor/chats/` — Cursor working files
- `worktrees/`, `.git/worktrees/` — git worktree dirs
- `old_modules*`, `old-*`, `*-archive`, `archive/` — manual archives
- `node_modules/`, `target/`, `dist/`, `build/` — build outputs
- `.venv/`, `venv/`, `__pycache__/` — Python virtualenvs
- `.claude/`, `.gstack/` — plugin internals
- Any file matching `*.bak`, `*.old`, `*~`

User can override ("include archive/old-bugs.md anyway") via explicit path
in their dct-import invocation.

---

#### Edge case handling

##### Bilingual / mixed-language titles

Polish, English, mixed — preserve as-is. Do not translate, do not strip
language markers. Example: `"Parser crashes / Parser się wywala"` stays
as the title unchanged.

##### Composite files (plan + checkboxes + narrative)

When a file clearly mixes formats, pick the dominant one and note the
mixed nature in the user's review table ("composite: plan-as-parent with
embedded checkboxes"). Usually "plan-as-parent" wins for 500+ line docs.

##### Done-status recognition

A sub-task is DONE when ANY of these hold:
- `[x]` or `[X]` prefix
- `✅` marker anywhere in the line
- Literal `**DONE**`, `STATUS: DONE`, `[DONE]`, `(done)`, `— done`
- Line struck through with `~~text~~`

##### No sprint / no plan / no checkboxes

If the file is pure prose without structure, offer to import as a single
`item_type="idea"` with the file content as description (truncated to
~1000 chars with link to full file path).

---

#### Rules

- **Language.** A quoted question, option, screen or report fixes what it
  says, not its wording: write it in the language of the conversation. Keep
  unchanged: identifiers, commands, paths, file contents, commit messages,
  changelog entries, short titles and anything shown verbatim.
The common consent boundary is the exact readable proposal before the user's explicit response. A selected default, timeout, silence, unattended run, old handoff or generated proposal is never approval. Changed scope requires a fresh concrete preview; reuse unchanged explicit consent already given. A report is not a consent request. Keep every proposal word visible before acceptance; hidden thinking, truncated content and a reference to an unavailable screen do not suffice.

Use the current host's eligible consent UI when it exposes complete previews; otherwise show the full decision material in visible text and ask for the explicit reply. Workflow references to dialog previews/Details pages mean the same complete readable content, translated to the current host's supported presentation. Never depend on hidden thinking, omitted pages or a Plan-only/optional-question-only permission tool.
- **Plan-like files → `ingest_plan_file`** — v0.2 pipeline owns ULID injection
  and first-import state semantics. Do not re-implement these inline.
- **Issue-like / changelog files → v0.1 items / changelog path** — unchanged,
  uses Pattern Catalog below.
- **Plan-like ingest DOES modify source files** — it injects HTML-comment
  ULID anchors. Users should know this (show diff option if they're unsure).
  Other formats: NEVER modify source files.
- **Provenance notes are mandatory for v0.1 items** — every legacy-path
  item gets `add_note("Imported from <file> on <date>")`. Plan-like entries
  have `plans.source_file` + `plans.imported_at` which serve the same role.
- **Respect stale-file skip list** — do not even offer those to the user.
- **One file, one format** — pick dominant; note composites for the user.
- **Changelog missing is OK** — skip gracefully, never error out.
- **Ambiguities are NEVER silent** — always flag and ask.


Discover only tools needed by the selected branch, using the current host's available discovery mechanism. Invoke tools with separate top-level parameters from their actual descriptions; illustrative `mcp__dct__` prefixes name DCT tools, not a requirement for one host's namespace. An unavailable operation is a readable capability refusal, never a reason for direct SQL or ad hoc Python writes.

Use the available MCP discovery mechanism. No client-specific discovery tool, task mirror, hooks or publisher is assumed.

## `/dct-init` fallback

### dct-init — bootstrap or register

One entry point for dct setup. Replaces the split mental model of
`dct init` (global, once) + `dct project add` (per-project, manual).

This is often the owner's FIRST contact with dct, so it leads by the hand:
the probes run silently, then ONE dialog explains what dct does and what
registering changes, shows what was detected instead of asking for it, and
asks only what the owner really chooses — each option saying in plain words
what it does and why. Everything the owner reads before answering travels
through the supported host presentation (Rules: exact readable consent).

#### Workflow

##### Step 1: Probe global bootstrap state

Identify the actual client, then use its supported `dct integrate status <client> --json` and `dct doctor --client <client> --json` diagnostics. A generic MCP connection does not prove installed skills, hooks or publishing. For a packaged client, offer its full repair only after showing exact effects and receiving Repair consent; re-probe afterwards. Missing/outdated owned reference can be repaired; foreign/edited content remains untouched with path/remedy. Valid JSON on exit 1 is still a diagnosis; absent reference JSON means unknown, not foreign. A reference problem alone does not block registration. Without a supported adapter, give the manual MCP registration/reconnect next step and report the limitation, never invent a client repair or use Claude installation on another client. Interactive `dct init` runs only in the owner's terminal and currently installs Claude; package upgrade is separate from integration repair.

##### Step 2: Probe current project registration (before any setup question)

Call `mcp__dct__list_projects`. Let `cwd = os.getcwd()`.

Canonicalize the actual checkout and stored paths (`os.path.realpath` semantics).
Match: for each project row, check if `cwd == row.path` or
`cwd.startswith(row.path + "/")`. Longest-prefix wins (use
`get_project_by_path` semantics).

If matched — the project is already set up: read its configuration and
SHOW it; nothing is reconfigured (no allowlist edit, no script generated or
changed, no registration). Read-only, in parallel:

- the current client integration status from Step 1; report permission limitations without assuming a Claude allowlist.
- the version sync — Step 3's probe: `scripts/dct-version-sync.sh` (with or
  without the dct sentinel), else `scripts/version-sync.sh` (the release
  runs it as the version sync), else none;
- the commit-line preferences — the row's `commit_co_authored_by` and
  `commit_session_link`: on / off / not answered (null).

```
✓ Already registered as `<slug>` — current_version=<v>, path=<path>
  Client setup: <actual current-client status>
  Version sync:  scripts/dct-version-sync.sh (dct template)
  Commit lines:  Co-Authored-By on · session link off
  Change the version: `dct project set-version <slug> <v>` · items: track-list
```

The other states, one line each: "Version sync:
scripts/dct-version-sync.sh without the dct sentinel", "Version sync:
scripts/version-sync.sh — run by every release as the version sync, before
you approve" or "Version sync: none — `dct project version-sync-script
<slug>` adds one"; "Commit lines: not answered"; when the reference is
not `current`, its `Reference:` line from Step 1.

Then stop: the status is the final text of the turn. The one exception: a
commit-line preference that is not answered (the project was registered
before dct stored them) — ask the commit-lines question of Step 5 once,
alone in its dialog, and store the answer; nothing else is asked, and the
status follows as the final text.

If no match: continue to Step 3.

##### Step 3: Probe silently — no question yet

Read-only, in parallel; the owner sees nothing of this but the dialog of
Step 5:

1. **Current-client permissions**: Probe only the actual host permission capability; if none is supported, report it without assuming Claude settings.
2. **Conflicting project artifacts**:
   Inspect the current host actual workflow/skill search locations when supported; unknown discovery behavior is a named limitation.
   Read `AGENTS.md`, applicable `AGENTS.override.md`, `CLAUDE.md`,
   `CLAUDE.local.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` and applicable private instruction
   paths for existing trackers (Linear/Jira/TODOS.md/ISSUES.md) or shadowing.
   Report their paths and suggest the explicit import workflow when useful.
   Merely mentioning another tracker is never authorization to edit instructions.

3. **The version-sync script** (first match wins): `./scripts/dct-version-sync.sh`
   — line 2 (after the shebang) is the sentinel `# dct-version-sync template
   v1` → dct's own, nothing to ask; without it, or `./scripts/*version*.sh`
   / `./scripts/*bump*.sh` → an existing script of the project (Step 5,
   Q2); none → no script yet (Step 5, Q2).
4. **What to show instead of asking**: folder = CWD; slug =
   `basename(CWD)`, lowercased, non-alnum → `-`; name = the slug;
   `(detected_version, source_file)` = `dct.core.version.detect_version(folder)`.
5. **Tracking files** for the report's `Next:` line (Step 7).

What the version-sync script is, for the questions below: dct's release
(`dct release prepare`, behind `release`) runs the committed
`./scripts/dct-version-sync.sh <version>` if present — it takes precedence —
else a script named exactly `./scripts/version-sync.sh`, automatically, with
no setting to switch it on — once, in an isolated temporary worktree — and
the owner approves the files it changes as the project's version-file
contract at the first release (`docs/release-workflow.md`).

**The script changes ONLY the version files** (the version fields of
`pyproject.toml`, `package.json`, `Cargo.toml`, …) and nothing else.
`prepare` runs it BEFORE the owner sees the release's consent screen, and
the isolated worktree is not a sandbox: the script can still reach the
network, the user's home directory or any absolute path. Never wrap a
release, publish or deploy command (an existing `release.sh`, a `release`
make / just / task target, `npm publish`, `cargo publish`, `twine upload`,
a tag or a push) as the version sync — it could publish before anyone
approved the release. A script that writes into the checkout itself is
refused by prepare, with the changed files named.

##### Step 4: Conflicts — only when Step 3 found one

If zero conflicts: nothing to ask; report no current-client artifact conflicts with global dct.

Otherwise ONE decision interaction before the registration dialog, one question
per conflict (at most 4; more → the next dialog), the conflict's details
(path, what it shadows or duplicates) as the preview of its first option:

  question: f"Conflict: {<describe>} (found at {<path>})"
  header:   "Conflict"
  options:
    - "Keep local" — preserve it and report the actual host precedence; no write
    - "Remove local (backup to <path>.bak) and use global dct" — rename file, keep backup
    - "Inspect integration options" — report the exact proposed hook/skill change; instruction files remain unchanged unless the owner separately authorizes their edit
    - "Skip — decide later" — leave the conflict, proceed to Step 5

Only an explicitly approved local skill/hook conflict may be renamed or integrated. Instruction-file conflicts are report-only here; never rename or edit them merely because another tracker is mentioned.

Each decision is recorded for the Step 7 report: "✓ Handled N conflicts:
<list>".

##### Step 5: The registration dialog — ONE decision interaction

Up to four questions in ONE dialog. A question is asked only when it is a
real choice; what was detected is shown, never asked. Plain words: no
"slug", "template" or "sentinel" in a question or an option.

**Q1 — register** (always):

  question: "Register <folder name> in dct?"
  header: "dct"
  options:
    - "Register" (recommended) — its preview:
      ```
      dct keeps this project's work in one place:
        items      tasks, bugs, ideas — track
        changelog  what changed, as you work — clog
        handoffs   where you stopped — handoff, pickup
        releases   version, changelog, tag, push — release

      Registering stores in dct's own database
      (nothing in this folder changes):
        name     proj-a
        folder   /tmp/proj-a
        version  0.2.1 (read from pyproject.toml)
      ```
      No version detected: "version  none yet — your first release proposes 0.1.0".
    - "Change the name or version" — "Say what — I ask again with the new values."
    - "Cancel" — "Nothing is registered and nothing changes."

**Q2 — the version file** — the cases of Step 3's script probe:

**Case 1 — dct's own script** (the sentinel is there): no question; the
report says it is in place.

**Case 2 — an existing script of the project**: read it first, to see which
version files it edits. It is never wrapped: the dct script carries its own
version-file edits, so it is safe to run before the consent screen whatever
the other script does. Branch on the path found:

- exactly `scripts/version-sync.sh` — dct's release already runs it
  automatically as the version sync (when there is no
  `scripts/dct-version-sync.sh`, which takes precedence), BEFORE the owner's
  consent screen, so it must change only the version files. Say so plainly:
    question: "Every release runs your scripts/version-sync.sh before you approve it. Keep it that way?"
    header: "Version sync"
    options:
      - "Add scripts/dct-version-sync.sh from dct — it takes precedence, so the release no longer runs scripts/version-sync.sh (recommended)"
      - "Keep it — the release runs scripts/version-sync.sh as it is (it must change only the version files)"
      - "Skip — configure nothing now; the release still runs scripts/version-sync.sh"
- Any other name (`scripts/bump-version.sh`, …) — the release never runs
  it:
    question: f"Every release could also write the new version for you. Add dct's own script next to {script_path}?"
    header: "Version sync"
    options:
      - "Add scripts/dct-version-sync.sh — it edits only the version files {script_path} edits (recommended)"
      - "Keep standalone — the release workflow bumps no files; the project releases those files with its own tool"
      - "Skip for now"

  "Add" writes the script with `dct project version-sync-script <slug>
  --kind <the version file the existing script edits>` (Step 6). When that
  file is not one dct can edit (VERSION, pyproject.toml, package.json,
  Cargo.toml, src-tauri/tauri.conf.json), say so and leave it out of the
  options. The original script stays untouched.

**Case 3 — no script yet**:
- a version file was detected (`source_file`):
    question: f"Should every release write the new version into {source_file} for you?"
    header: "Version sync"
    options:
      - "Yes — add scripts/dct-version-sync.sh (recommended)" — its preview,
        the version line of `source_file` filled in:
        ```
        dct adds one small file: scripts/dct-version-sync.sh

        What it does: every release writes the new version into pyproject.toml — only this line:
          version = "0.2.1"  →  version = "0.3.0"
        It never builds, tags, pushes or publishes anything.

        When it runs: once per release, before you approve it, in a temporary copy of the project; the release screen shows the change it makes. It works once it is committed — commit takes it along with your work.

        Why: the released package then carries the same version as its tag and its changelog section.
        ```
      - f"No — I change {source_file} myself" — its preview:
        ```
        Releases still write the changelog section, the tag and the push; pyproject.toml keeps 0.2.1 until you change it yourself.

        You can add the script later:
          dct project version-sync-script <slug>
        ```
- no version file at all: no question — there is nothing to write into;
  the report says so.

Generating never overwrites an existing `scripts/dct-version-sync.sh`:
`dct project version-sync-script` refuses when the file exists, and only
the owner's answer to Case 2 changes anything there.

**Q3 — commit lines** (a new project, and a registered project whose
preferences are not answered yet — Step 2). Which lines commit adds to
every commit of this project. Asked once; once stored, never asked again:
commit applies the stored answer without asking.

  question: "Which lines should commits in <project> carry? I ask once — commit applies your answer to every commit."
  header: "Commit lines"
  options:
    - "Co-Authored-By, no session link (recommended)" — "Each commit names the AI assistant as co-author: a standard git line, visible in the history."
    - "Neither" — "Commits carry no line about the assistant."
    - "Both — Co-Authored-By and a link to the assistant session" — "The link points to this conversation — never in a public repository, the conversation can hold private content."
    - "Session link only"

The project's own rules win: read them from the project's instruction
  files on disk at the repository top level — `AGENTS.md` and, where the
  project still keeps rules there, `CLAUDE.md` / `CLAUDE.local.md` (also
  `.claude/CLAUDE.md`); a project with only `AGENTS.md` is read the same
  way. Never rely on the client's automatic `@import` expansion: a line
  `@<path>` in one of them means: read `<path>` yourself. When the project's
  own rules in any of them forbid a trailer, it is never written whatever
  is stored, never offered as an option to approve again, and stored as
  `off` when the preferences are asked. dct's own repository forbids a
  session link (OSS hygiene, in its `AGENTS.md`).

Offer a permission preference only if supported by this host and its exact effect is known; otherwise omit it and report the limitation.

**"Change the name or version"** → the owner says what in plain words
("name My App", "version 1.0.0", "short name my-app", "folder ~/code/app");
apply it and ask the dialog again with the new values in the "Register"
preview. **"Cancel"** → nothing is written, whatever the other answers say.

##### Step 6: Execute — after "Register"

1. ```
   dct project add <slug> <path> --name "<name>" --version <vX.Y.Z>
   ```
   Always pass the version the "Register" preview showed: without it `dct
   project add` stores the version it detects itself, so there is no "no
   version" choice when one is detected (change it later with `dct project
   set-version`). With no version detected or given, leave `--version` out.
   Run via the available shell tool in the current checkout. Verify with `mcp__dct__list_projects` — the new slug must
   appear.
2. Q2 "Yes" / "Add" → `dct project version-sync-script <slug>` (Case 2:
   with `--kind <file>`). It writes the script from dct's packaged template
   with the block of that file switched on, prints the one line it will
   change, and refuses to overwrite an existing script.
3. Q3 → store the answer (on = the line is added, off = never added):
   ```
   dct project trailers <slug> --co-authored-by on|off --session-link on|off
   ```
Apply only the supported host permission preference explicitly approved on the draft. Otherwise perform no permission write.

##### Step 7: Final report

The final text of the turn:

```
✓ Bootstrap:    <actual current-client MCP/assets/hook capability status>
✓ Client setup: <actual current-client status>
✓ Project:      <slug> registered at <path>, version <v>
✓ Version sync: scripts/dct-version-sync.sh writes the version into pyproject.toml — commit it (commit) before the first release
✓ Commit lines: Co-Authored-By on · session link off
⚠ Reference:    <actual doctor state/path/remedy, only when not current>
  Next: dct-import (tracking files found) · track to add the first item
```

The `Reference:` line appears only when the reference is not `current`
(Step 1: missing, outdated, foreign or unknown, with that state's line). The report ends the skill —
no closing question. The `Next:` line is a
hint, not a menu: name `dct-import` first when the project path holds
plausible tracking files (any of `ROADMAP.md`, `TODOS.md`, `BACKLOG.md`,
`SPRINT*.md`, `PLAN*.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `changelog.md`,
`docs/plans/*.md`, `docs/specs/*.md`), else `track` alone. Registration
alone leaves an empty project (`pickup` and `track-list` return
nothing), so the hint says where to go — the owner runs it when they want.

#### Rules

- **Language.** A quoted question, option, screen or report fixes what it
  says, not its wording: write it in the language of the conversation. Keep
  unchanged: identifiers, commands, paths, file contents, commit messages,
  changelog entries, short titles and anything shown verbatim.
The common consent boundary is the exact readable proposal before the user's explicit response. A selected default, timeout, silence, unattended run, old handoff or generated proposal is never approval. Changed scope requires a fresh concrete preview; reuse unchanged explicit consent already given. A report is not a consent request. Keep every proposal word visible before acceptance; hidden thinking, truncated content and a reference to an unavailable screen do not suffice.

Use the current host's eligible consent UI when it exposes complete previews; otherwise show the full decision material in visible text and ask for the explicit reply. Workflow references to dialog previews/Details pages mean the same complete readable content, translated to the current host's supported presentation. Never depend on hidden thinking, omitted pages or a Plan-only/optional-question-only permission tool.
- **Idempotent probes first.** Safe to re-run at any time — an already
  registered project gets its configuration status (Step 2) and no setup
  question; only a commit-line preference that is not answered yet is
  asked, once.
- **Show what was detected; ask only real choices.** Folder, name and
  version are shown in the "Register" preview, never asked one by one;
  "Change the name or version" covers the unusual case.
- **Single source of truth for bootstrap.** The skill never
  re-implements MCP/skill/hook installation and never runs `dct init`
  (interactive — the owner runs it in a terminal) or `dct upgrade` (it also
  upgrades the package). A partial current-client integration or a missing
  owned reference is repaired with its client-specific command from Step 1,
  only after the owner's Repair answer.
- **Single source of truth for registration and the script.** Skill calls
  `dct project add` and `dct project version-sync-script`; never writes the
  DB directly and never copies or hand-edits a version-sync script.
- **No overwrite of foreign content.** Report MCP/config conflicts through
  current-client diagnostics; installer ownership rules remain binding.


Discover only tools needed by the selected branch, using the current host's available discovery mechanism. Invoke tools with separate top-level parameters from their actual descriptions; illustrative `mcp__dct__` prefixes name DCT tools, not a requirement for one host's namespace. An unavailable operation is a readable capability refusal, never a reason for direct SQL or ad hoc Python writes.

Use the available MCP discovery mechanism. No client-specific discovery tool, task mirror, hooks or publisher is assumed.

## `/handoff` fallback

### handoff — Session Handoff

Finalize a coding session by (a) marking which items belong to the next sprint
and (b) optionally writing a prompt for the next session to pick up.

Discover only tools needed by the selected branch, using the current host's available discovery mechanism. Invoke tools with separate top-level parameters from their actual descriptions; illustrative `mcp__dct__` prefixes name DCT tools, not a requirement for one host's namespace. An unavailable operation is a readable capability refusal, never a reason for direct SQL or ad hoc Python writes.

Use the available MCP discovery mechanism. No client-specific discovery tool, task mirror, hooks or publisher is assumed.

#### Workflow

##### Step 1: Preflight (ONE parallel message)

Gather all state in a single parallel message:
- `mcp__dct__get_context_snapshot(project="")` — CWD auto-detect; returns all
  active sprints (`sprint.active_sprints`, `primary_sprint_id`), member items
  with `cp`, their `checkpoints`, `stale_in_progress`, pending `gates`, live
  `decisions`, `recent_changes` and `summary`. Gates and decisions FEED THE
  DRAFT: an unresolved gate or open ADR question belongs in the handoff text.
- If native task/plan mirroring is installed and actual host events were observed, inspect the relevant mirror item deliberately. A generic MCP connection or conversation plan is not evidence of an active task mirror. With no mirror capability, omit the mirror decision line and probe.

**Fallback only when project is unresolved** (`get_context_snapshot` errors
because CWD is not a registered project): `mcp__dct__list_projects()` +
decision interaction ("Which project is this handoff for?" → slugs + "Cancel"),
then re-run preflight with the chosen slug.

##### Step 2: The draft and ONE question (the draft travels inside the dialog)

Auto-draft at once — no setup questions. Draft 2-4 sentences: what was
accomplished (resolved items / recent changelog), what's next (first 1-2
sprint items), any open design questions — plus pending GATES and open
DECISIONS from the snapshot (the next session must honor them without
transcript access). An empty project (no open or recent items) still gets a
short draft that says so.

The sprint and scope decisions are LINES OF THE DRAFT, with their defaults — `Sprint: unchanged` and `Scope: none` — never questions of their own:

- **`Sprint: unchanged`** — the default. Sprints are MULTI-SESSION (ADR #57):
  a handoff designates the NEXT SESSION'S SLICE, it does not re-plan the
  sprint. Add a `Could add:` line with the candidates — P1 open items not yet
  in the sprint, the top few P2 open items with existing checkpoints, still-open
  items from `recent_changes` — so the user can take them through "Change".
- **`Scope: none`** — the default; a scope tag only disambiguates parallel
  sessions.
- **`Native tasks: keep #N`** — ONLY when the Step 1 host probe found an actual mirror item: keep it for the next pickup unless an approved Change resolves it or promotes its checkpoints.

The approval is one supported decision interaction on the exact draft. The presentation rule below determines eligible UI or complete visible text; never ask acceptance of hidden or truncated content.

The screen is the draft with its decision lines — the prompt as written, one
line per paragraph (the dialog wraps it; what is saved is the prompt word for
word), each decision line under 60 characters:

```
--- BEGIN DRAFT ---
<the full prompt text, verbatim>
--- END DRAFT ---
Sprint: unchanged
Could add: #22, #6 (P1, not in the sprint)
Scope: none
Native tasks: keep #31            (only when the probe found one)

--- BEGIN CONTEXT SUMMARY ---  (only when one was drafted)
<the full context_summary, verbatim>
--- END CONTEXT SUMMARY ---
```

ONE decision interaction:
- question: "Save this handoff for the next session?"
- options:
  - "Save" (recommended) — its preview: the screen (its page 1 when the
    screen is longer than 15 lines)
  - "Change — I will say what" — prompt text, sprint, scope or native tasks
  - "Cancel — write nothing"
- A screen longer than 15 lines is split into pages of at most 15 lines, and
  the dialog gets a second single-select question, "Details", with one option
  per page ("Page 2 of 3"), each with that page as its preview. Every word of
  the draft and of the context_summary is on a page — nothing is shortened. A
  draft that needs more than 4 pages is too long for a handoff: shorten it
  before asking.
- The question text and the option labels and descriptions carry none of the
  draft: it is only in the previews.

**"Change"** → collect what to change in a free-text follow-up (in plain
words: "add #22", "cut #7", "replan to 22, 21, 6", "scope g1", "resolve the native
tasks", "sprint only, no prompt", new prompt text), apply it to the draft, then
ask Step 2's dialog again with the revised draft in its previews — the user
must read the revision before saving it too. A sprint change shows on the
`Sprint:` line as `add #22, #6` / `cut #7` / `replace → #22, #21, #6
(removing #7; resolved members stay as history)`. Removing a resolved /
wont_fix member is REFUSED by the server — terminal members are the sprint's
completion history, not scope (the escape hatch is `remove_item_from_sprint`).
There is NO "empty sprint" change: emptying a sprint is `clear_sprint`'s job
and `handoff_work` rejects an empty replace.

**Target sprint** — when a Change modifies the sprint AND
`summary.active_sprint_count >= 2`, ask "Which active sprint gets these
items?" (one option per `sprint.active_sprints` entry: `#id (code) — name,
size N`) before asking again, and show the answer as a `Target sprint:` line.
`handoff_work` REFUSES to guess among several actives (and so does every
current-sprint helper).

**"Cancel"** → nothing is written: no handoff, no sprint change.

##### Step 3: Finale (ONE atomic call, after "Save")

```
mcp__dct__handoff_work(
    prompt=<saved text>,
    created_by="<known_actor_identity>",
    project="",
    item_ids=<"__keep__" (default) | "22,21,6" ONLY for a conscious replan>,
    add_item_ids=<"22,6" when the draft says "add">,
    remove_item_ids=<"7" when the draft says "cut">,
    sprint=<id-or-code, ONLY when the draft has a Target sprint line>,
    scope=<scope or "">,
    context_summary=<the approved context_summary, verbatim, or "" when none was drafted>,
)
```

Every line of the saved draft maps to an argument, so nothing the user
approved is lost: the prompt → `prompt`, the `CONTEXT SUMMARY` block →
`context_summary`, `Sprint:` → `item_ids` / `add_item_ids` /
`remove_item_ids`, `Target sprint:` → `sprint`, `Scope:` → `scope`,
`Native tasks:` → its own calls below. The context_summary is passed verbatim —
exactly the text on the draft the user saved; never shorten or regenerate it
after "Save" (the next pickup shows it as written).

Sprint membership and the handoff row are written in ONE DB transaction —
a failed sprint write leaves NO handoff (and vice versa), so there is no
ordering to manage and no partial state to report. Mapping from the `Sprint:`
line: "unchanged" → send nothing (`item_ids="__keep__"`, the default, no
membership write); "add" / "cut" → `add_item_ids` / `remove_item_ids` (they
may be combined); "replace" → `item_ids=<CSV>`, which is mutually exclusive
with the additive pair. **NEVER send `item_ids=""`** — an empty replace errors
by design (emptying a sprint is `clear_sprint`'s job).

The `Native tasks:` line: "keep" → nothing; "resolve" →
`resolve_item(id, status="resolved", resolution="session ephemeral, archived on handoff")`;
"promote" → `promote_checkpoint_to_item` per checkpoint (discover it first).

Branch: the saved draft says **"sprint only, no prompt"** → `handoff_work`
does not apply (prompt is required by design). If the sprint was kept too,
there is nothing to write at all. Otherwise map the `Sprint:` line to the
existing additive tools, one item at a time — an "add" adds, a "cut" cuts, and
nothing else is touched:

- **No active sprint** → "add #22" → `mcp__dct__add_item_to_current_sprint(22,
  project)`, which creates the current sprint; a "cut" has nothing to cut —
  stop and say so ("no active sprint, nothing to cut"); a "replace" →
  `set_sprint`, below.
- **One active sprint** → "add" → `mcp__dct__add_item_to_current_sprint(item_id,
  project)`; "cut" → `mcp__dct__remove_item_from_current_sprint(item_id,
  project)`, only for an OPEN member (the snapshot's `sprint.items` status) —
  a resolved / wont_fix member is the sprint's history: stop and say so
  instead of removing it.
- **Several active sprints** → the `Target sprint:` line names the sprint (the
  Target sprint question above); "add" → `mcp__dct__assign_item_to_sprint(item_id,
  sprint_id)`, "cut" → `mcp__dct__remove_item_from_sprint(item_id, sprint_id)`
  (both deferred — discover them only in this branch, with the two
  current-sprint tools when needed). A missing or ambiguous target stops
  readably — "several active sprints; which one gets #22?" — it is never
  guessed.
- **"replace"** — only when the saved draft says `replace → …` (a replacement
  the user accepted) → `mcp__dct__set_sprint(project, item_ids=<the listed
  ids>)` with no active or one active sprint. With several active sprints
  `set_sprint` errors and no tool replaces a chosen one without a handoff:
  stop and say that this replace needs a prompt (`handoff_work` with
  `sprint=…`).

Never compute a full list for `set_sprint` from a read of the sprint plus
the change (read + replace) — an item another session added meanwhile would
be dropped. An add or a cut is never a replace.

Remember the returned `handoff_id`.

##### Step 4: Report

```
✓ Handoff #N zapisany
  Sprint: 3 itemy (#22, #21, #6)
  Scope: sprint-v0.2
  Prompt: "Zacznij od #22..." (142 chars)

Next session: pickup
```

#### Rules

- **Language.** A quoted question, option, screen or report fixes what it
  says, not its wording: write it in the language of the conversation. Keep
  unchanged: identifiers, commands, paths, file contents, commit messages,
  changelog entries, short titles and anything shown verbatim.
The common consent boundary is the exact readable proposal before the user's explicit response. A selected default, timeout, silence, unattended run, old handoff or generated proposal is never approval.
