Changed scope requires a fresh concrete preview; reuse unchanged explicit consent already given. A report is not a consent request. Keep every proposal word visible before acceptance; hidden thinking, truncated content and a reference to an unavailable screen do not suffice.

Use the current host's eligible consent UI when it exposes complete previews; otherwise show the full decision material in visible text and ask for the explicit reply. Workflow references to dialog previews/Details pages mean the same complete readable content, translated to the current host's supported presentation. Never depend on hidden thinking, omitted pages or a Plan-only/optional-question-only permission tool.
- Never modify sprint membership without the user's "Save" on a draft whose
  `Sprint:` line shows the change. The default is "unchanged" — a sprint spans
  sessions (ADR #57); a handoff designates the next slice, it does not re-plan
  by default.
- Terminal (resolved / wont_fix) members are the sprint's completion history:
  a replace leaves them in place and a remove of one is refused. Never try to
  "clean up" a sprint by dropping resolved items — that destroys
  `sprint_completion`.
- Never write a handoff before the user's "Save" on the draft the dialog
  showed (Step 2: the draft in the previews, then the one question).
- **Long text never goes into the question text or an option label or
  description** — they stay short and self-contained. The handoff prompt and
  the context_summary the user must read are previews of that dialog (pages
  when longer than 15 lines), word for word.
- `created_by` MUST be non-empty and truthful; the true client alone is sufficient. Add model/session/link only from the host and project/time only under the shared known-component rule below (`handoff_work` refuses blanks).
- With several active sprints, the target sprint is a USER decision (the
  Target sprint question after a sprint Change) — `handoff_work` errors rather
  than guessing, and so do the current-sprint helpers (`set_sprint`,
  `clear_sprint`, `add_item_to_current_sprint`,
  `remove_item_from_current_sprint`). Never pick one silently.
- Unknown/foreign item ids make `handoff_work` fail atomically (nothing
  written) — report the error verbatim and re-ask, don't retry blindly.
- Round-trip budget: preflight = 1 parallel message (2 calls), finale = 1 call.
  If you find yourself sequencing `set_sprint` → `create_handoff`, you are off
  the rails (the "sprint only, no prompt" branch writes no handoff at all,
  and uses `set_sprint` only for an accepted replace).


Use truthful actor identity in `created_by` and `consumed_by`. Only the true client is mandatory. Model, session identifier and session link are included only when supplied by the host; never invent them.

A project suffix is included only from a prior successful DCT response or an explicit user-supplied slug, never a directory, worktree or task-title guess. UTC is included only from an actual provided clock, known host time context or a time tool; no approximate time. Otherwise omit unknown components entirely, including project and time: never fill them with `unknown`, `?`, `0000` or guessed values. Server-created `created_at` / `consumed_at` timestamps remain separate ledger facts.

Use `<known_actor_identity>` in calls. A client-only identity such as `Codex` or `Claude Code` is sufficient when nothing else is known. Full-format example, ONLY when all components are known: `<true client>[-<host-supplied model>] @ <verified project slug> <actual UTC time>`. The same known-component rule applies to creation and consumption.

No mandatory extra lookup or preflight is added to AUTO pickup. Preserve its one-call path; do not obtain a slug by a guessed directory mapping, call a writer to bypass a read-only schema refusal, or require a clock lookup merely to fill an optional component. A status question remains a pure read with no `consumed_by` required.

Identify the actual assistant client. Capability and identity information must come from the running host.

When a shared read (`get_context_snapshot` or `pickup_work(consume="false")`, CLI `dct pickup --consume never`) refuses with SchemaNotReady, explain that setup or a schema upgrade is required. Propose `dct db upgrade` with explicit consent, then retry the original read only after that migration succeeds. Never invoke an unrelated writer to trigger a hidden migration. A SQLite reader may create WAL/SHM sidecars; it does not initialize the database, change journal mode, schema or data. Do not infer this guarantee for other list/get tools.


#### CLI equivalent

`dct handoff create --prompt-file - --add-items 22,6 --scope g1 --context-summary-file summary.md` saves the approved prompt/context summary (`--remove-items` cuts, `--items` replaces; omit all three to keep the sprint). `--context-summary "…"` is the short inline alternative. Only one file argument may read stdin.

## `/pickup` fallback

### pickup — Session Resume

Open a new session by loading the previous session's handoff prompt + sprint
state in ONE composed call, then start on the handoff's next step — or show
the handoff inside a dialog and ask, when there is something to decide.

Discover only tools needed by the selected branch, using the current host's available discovery mechanism. Invoke tools with separate top-level parameters from their actual descriptions; illustrative `mcp__dct__` prefixes name DCT tools, not a requirement for one host's namespace. An unavailable operation is a readable capability refusal, never a reason for direct SQL or ad hoc Python writes.

Use the available MCP discovery mechanism. No client-specific discovery tool, task mirror, hooks or publisher is assumed.

#### Workflow

##### Step 1: One composed call (CWD auto-detect)

What the user said decides whether a handoff is consumed:

- **An instruction to continue** — on an unambiguous "continue" / "pickup" /
  "resume" (or `pickup` itself) the call consumes the single matching
  handoff (AUTO mode). All three commands have the same accepted consume behavior.
- **A status question** — "where were we", "what's next", "what's the state"
  → `pickup_work(project="", consume="false")`, a PURE READ, no `consumed_by`
  needed: report the state and say that a handoff is waiting and that
  "continue" picks it up. A request to only look ("show the handoff but keep
  it", an audit) is the same read.
- A word the user merely quotes or mentions ("what does "continue" do?") is
  not a command; only a request addressed to you counts.

```
mcp__dct__pickup_work(project="", consume="",
                      consumed_by="<known_actor_identity>")
```

`consume=""` is the server's AUTO mode. With exactly ONE matching unconsumed
handoff it consumes that handoff in the same transaction, without a question —
an unambiguous "continue" / "pickup" already says to pick it up — and returns
it as `picked_up` with its FULL prompt (`consumed: true`). With several
matching handoffs it consumes nothing and returns them in the `handoff`
section (Step 2 asks which); with none, nothing is written. When the user
names a workstream, pass `scope=<tag>` so only its handoffs match.

One call returns everything Step 2 needs:

- **`picked_up`** — the consumed handoff row with its FULL prompt (and
  `context_summary`), or `null` when nothing was consumed.
- **`handoff.latest`** — the newest matching handoff still unconsumed after
  the call, with its FULL prompt; `handoff.others` carries 200-char previews
  of every OTHER unconsumed handoff — of any scope, capped (`truncated:
  true` when rows were left out).
- **How many match** — with a scope, `handoff.scope_matched` (only this
  workstream's unconsumed handoffs); without a scope, the global
  `pending_count` of the `handoff` section (all of them). Never branch on `pending_count` when a scope was given.
- **`sprint`** — ALL active sprints (`active_sprints`, `primary_sprint_id`),
  member items with `cp`, their `checkpoints` (the next pending checkpoint is
  readable directly), `stale_in_progress`.
- **`gates`** — pending gate checkpoints of EVERY open item, in a sprint or
  not (`in_current_sprint` tells which); **`decisions`** —
  live ADRs/open questions with previews; **`summary`** — sprint_size,
  sprint_completion, handoffs_pending, gates_pending.

**Fallback only when project is unresolved** (CWD not registered →
`pickup_work` errors): call `mcp__dct__list_projects()` and ask via
decision interaction ("Which project are we working on?" → slugs + "Cancel"),
then re-call `pickup_work(<slug>, ...)` the same way.

##### Step 2: Start, or show the handoff inside the dialog

A handoff the user must read before choosing must be completely visible in the supported UI or the visible-text fallback, according to the presentation rule below.

- **The auto-start path — no question follows** (one handoff consumed on an
  unambiguous "continue", Step 4 below): the user already read and saved this
  handoff at handoff. Check its next step (`get_item`, the pending `gates`)
  and start on it in the same turn; the Step 5 report names the handoff and
  the step. "Show the handoff" prints it as the final text of a turn. When the
  check finds the step stale, contradictory or unclear, Step 4's question
  carries the handoff in its previews.
- **The user must decide** (several matching handoffs, Step 3): each handoff
  is the preview of its option.

A handoff as a screen — header line, then the prompt verbatim, one line per
paragraph (the dialog wraps it), then its `context_summary` when present:

```
Handoff #N [scope: X] from <created_at> by <created_by> — consumed
--- BEGIN HANDOFF PROMPT ---
<the full prompt text, verbatim>
--- END HANDOFF PROMPT ---
```

**Several matching handoffs** (nothing consumed; the count from Step 1 ≥ 2):
offer only the matching ones — with a scope, only handoffs of that scope,
never another workstream's. When `handoff.others` is truncated, or holds
fewer matching rows than the count says, the list is not complete: fetch it
first with `mcp__dct__list_handoffs(project="")` (unconsumed, previews; keep
only the matching scope). `handoff.latest` carries the full prompt; read the
full prompt of each other handoff you offer with `mcp__dct__get_handoff(M)` —
a read, without consuming it.

##### Step 3: Several handoffs — pick one after reading it

**ONE decision interaction, only "which handoff"** (never together with the
first action — that is decided only after the chosen handoff was read):
- question: "Which handoff do we continue? (N waiting)"
- options: "Continue #N" for each matching handoff, newest first, at most 3 —
  each with that handoff's screen as its preview; "None — start fresh". With
  more than 3, the question names the rest by id ("also #12, #9 — name one
  under Other").

A choice made from a text nobody could read is no consent to run its plan:

- **"Continue #N" on a handoff whose whole screen fit in its preview** (at
  most 15 lines) — an unambiguous instruction to continue a handoff the user
  has read in full → only now consume it:
  ```
  mcp__dct__pickup_work(project="", consume="true", handoff_id=N,
                        include="none",
                        consumed_by="<known_actor_identity>")
  ```
  `include="none"` keeps the consume cheap (Step 1 already delivered the
  state). Then Step 4.
- **"Continue #M" on a longer handoff** (its preview showed only page 1), or
  "show the older one" → nothing is consumed yet: ask ONE question
  "Continue handoff #M?" → "Continue #M" (preview: page 1) / "Back to the
  list" / "None — start fresh", with every page on its "Details" pages.
  Showing it stays a read; "Continue #M" here consumes it as above.
- **"None — start fresh"** → consume nothing; optionally `delete_handoff(id)`
  (deferred tool — load only if the user explicitly wants a discard).

##### Step 4: The first step — start it, or ask

After a handoff was consumed on an instruction to continue, read the next step
it names: an item id or a pending checkpoint. Check it against the CURRENT
state before acting — `mcp__dct__get_item(X)` (its status, its checkpoints)
and the pending `gates` of the snapshot.

- **The step is concrete and still current** (the item is open or
  in_progress, the checkpoint pending, no gate in its way, and nothing the
  user said in this session points elsewhere) → start on it at once, without
  a question, and say so: `Starting with #22 — "<next pending checkpoint>";
  tell me if you want something else.`
- **The step is stale, contradictory or unclear** (the item is resolved, the
  checkpoint done, a gate blocks it, two handoffs disagree, the user asked for
  something else, or no step is named) → ask the first action — ONE
  decision interaction, the consumed handoff's screen as the preview of its
  first option (pages when longer):
  - question: "First action for this session?"
  - options: "Open #<first-sprint-item> and start on its checkpoints" /
    "Review all sprint items first" / "Look at stale in_progress first (#X)" /
    "Something else — tell me what".

An old handoff is no new consent: a commit, a push, publishing a release or
any destructive step written in its text still waits for the user's own
instruction in this session (and for the consent the skill that performs it
asks for). The handoff names the work, not a permission — and it never
overrides what the user asks for now.

With no handoff at all (or "None — start fresh"), ask the first action the
same way. **Empty-sprint variants** — replace its options when the sprint is
empty:
- Sprint empty BUT open items exist: "Pick sprint items now — run handoff" / "Browse open items — track-list" / "Just start working — I'll tell you what".
- Sprint empty AND no open items: "Create the first item — run track" / "Import existing tracking data — run dct-import" / "Exit — not the right project".

The Step 5 report carries the sprint items as a compact table (from
`sprint.items`) plus summary: sprint_size, sprint_completion,
handoffs_pending, and the opened item's pending checkpoints (from
`sprint.checkpoints`) as the next-step plan.

##### Step 5: Report

```
✓ Picked up handoff #N (consumed) — "<first sentence of its prompt>"
  Sprint: 3 items, 1/3 done
  Starting with #22 — "Optimize MCP response format"
  Plan: 4 pending checkpoints in this item
  Waiting on you: #22 dogfood — "Owner verifies the acceptance scenario"
```

The first line names the consumed handoff by its id (`#N`): the consume
happened without a question, so this is where the user sees it. Consuming only
marks the handoff read — the row and its prompt stay in the ledger. Nothing
consumed → `✓ No handoff consumed` (or `left unconsumed` after a read-only
look).

**Waiting on you** — one line per pending gate whose condition is a person's
act (`dogfood`, `approval`, or a gate whose text names the user), from the
snapshot's `gates`, sprint or not: `#<item_id> <kind> — "<text>"`. These are
what only the user can close; list them even when nothing else is due, and
omit the line when there are none. Never complete such a gate here.

If the project has plans with pending checkpoints, mention that
**`plan-status` shows overall plan progress** — a good next call when planned
work is in flight.

#### Rules

- **Language.** A quoted question, option, screen or report fixes what it
  says, not its wording: write it in the language of the conversation. Keep
  unchanged: identifiers, commands, paths, file contents, commit messages,
  changelog entries, short titles and anything shown verbatim.
The common consent boundary is the exact readable proposal before the user's explicit response. A selected default, timeout, silence, unattended run, old handoff or generated proposal is never approval. Changed scope requires a fresh concrete preview; reuse unchanged explicit consent already given. A report is not a consent request. Keep every proposal word visible before acceptance; hidden thinking, truncated content and a reference to an unavailable screen do not suffice.

Use the current host's eligible consent UI when it exposes complete previews; otherwise show the full decision material in visible text and ask for the explicit reply. Workflow references to dialog previews/Details pages mean the same complete readable content, translated to the current host's supported presentation. Never depend on hidden thinking, omitted pages or a Plan-only/optional-question-only permission tool.
- **Long text never goes into the question text or an option label or
  description** — they stay short and self-contained. A handoff prompt or
  context_summary the user must read before deciding is a preview of that
  dialog (pages when longer than 15 lines), word for word. With no dialog
  (the auto-start path of Step 4) the work starts at once and the report
  names the handoff.
- **Two consumes, nothing else.** The Step 1 AUTO consume of the single
  matching handoff on an instruction to continue, and `consume="true",
  handoff_id=N` for the handoff the user chose to continue after reading it in
  full. A status question or a request to only look is `consume="false"`.
  Never auto-pick among several handoffs, and never consume one that was only
  previewed.
- Race note: a parallel session may consume the same handoff first. The AUTO
  consume then degrades to `consumed: false` (no error) — proceed with the
  fresh snapshot. An explicit `handoff_id` instead errors "not found or
  already consumed": report it verbatim, keep the plan you already read, and
  do NOT retry in a loop.
- On empty sprint + no handoffs, don't force-create a sprint — ask user what to do.
- Show resolved items (they surface via `summary.sprint_completion` and
  `recent_changes`) only as context, not as work candidates.
- `consumed_by` is non-empty on every call that may consume and follows the
  same known-component identity rule as `created_by` below. The true client
  alone suffices; project/time are optional facts, never guessed. A
  `consume="false"` read needs no identity.
- Round-trip budget: 1 dct call — the Step 1 call, with `get_item` batched
  after it. The several-handoffs branch adds what it needs: `list_handoffs`
  only for an incomplete list, `get_handoff` for each handoff shown in full,
  and the Step 3 consume. `review_sprint` is never needed here.


Use truthful actor identity in `created_by` and `consumed_by`. Only the true client is mandatory. Model, session identifier and session link are included only when supplied by the host; never invent them.

A project suffix is included only from a prior successful DCT response or an explicit user-supplied slug, never a directory, worktree or task-title guess. UTC is included only from an actual provided clock, known host time context or a time tool; no approximate time. Otherwise omit unknown components entirely, including project and time: never fill them with `unknown`, `?`, `0000` or guessed values. Server-created `created_at` / `consumed_at` timestamps remain separate ledger facts.

Use `<known_actor_identity>` in calls. A client-only identity such as `Codex` or `Claude Code` is sufficient when nothing else is known. Full-format example, ONLY when all components are known: `<true client>[-<host-supplied model>] @ <verified project slug> <actual UTC time>`. The same known-component rule applies to creation and consumption.

No mandatory extra lookup or preflight is added to AUTO pickup. Preserve its one-call path; do not obtain a slug by a guessed directory mapping, call a writer to bypass a read-only schema refusal, or require a clock lookup merely to fill an optional component. A status question remains a pure read with no `consumed_by` required.

Identify the actual assistant client. Capability and identity information must come from the running host.

When a shared read (`get_context_snapshot` or `pickup_work(consume="false")`, CLI `dct pickup --consume never`) refuses with SchemaNotReady, explain that setup or a schema upgrade is required. Propose `dct db upgrade` with explicit consent, then retry the original read only after that migration succeeds. Never invoke an unrelated writer to trigger a hidden migration. A SQLite reader may create WAL/SHM sidecars; it does not initialize the database, change journal mode, schema or data. Do not infer this guarantee for other list/get tools.

## `/plan-resolve-uncertain` fallback

### plan-resolve-uncertain — Classify Uncertain Plan Sections

This workflow is explicit-only. Use it when the user asks to classify indexed uncertain sections or accepts that named follow-up after import; a status question alone does not run it.

#### Workflow

##### Step 1: Project and selected plan

Resolve the explicit project or match the current checkout against registered project paths. Ask only if ambiguous. `list_plans(project=<slug>, status="active")` returns `{cols, rows}` with integer id and ULID. Select the plan the user named; several candidates require a choice. Use `get_plan(plan_id=<integer>)` and `list_plan_sections(plan_id=<integer>, section_type="uncertain", format="structured")` to show every selected section's integer id, ULID, depth and heading. No direct query, full-file rescan or anchor injection.

##### Step 2: One strategy decision on the exact table

Show the selected project's plan and full uncertain-section table through the presentation rule below. Offer:
- Resolve using configured rules/command.
- Review one-by-one (manual choice per section).
- Mark these listed sections as prose.
- Skip — leave uncertain.

Inspect the current classification configuration without changing it. Rules need no model. A configured command may invoke an external provider; show that actual provider/known model and the known cost basis, or say that cost is unknown. Never promise Claude/Haiku, invent prices or force a provider. Obtain explicit strategy consent before invoking a configured external command. Disabled or unavailable providers leave sections unresolved; offer the manual strategy only as a new explicit choice.

##### Step 3a: Configured batch

Call `resolve_uncertain_sections(plan_id=<integer>, project=<slug>)`.
CLI equivalent: `dct plan resolve-uncertain <plan-ulid> --project <slug> --json`.
MCP accepts integer primary keys only; CLI takes the explicit plan ULID with project guard. Retain `{resolved:[ids], unresolved:[{id,reason}], skipped:[{id,reason}], remaining_uncertain:n}`. The operation snapshots candidates, executes configured rules/command outside a write transaction and conditionally writes only still-live, unchanged, uncertain rows. Invalid plan/project/config refuses before invocation. Disabled/missing/failed command is a non-secret reason, never a made-up result. Preserve successful per-section progress after later failures; a retry targets only remaining uncertain rows.

##### Step 3b: Manual per section or the approved prose list

For each listed section the user chose, apply exactly the approved type via
`set_plan_section_type(section_id=<integer>, section_type=<type>, project=<slug>)`.
CLI equivalent: `dct plan set-section-type <section-ulid> <type> --project <slug> --json`.
Types: sprint, phase, task, block, milestone, decision, prose, changelog, adr_section, reference, generic, uncertain. Skip writes nothing. A bulk prose choice uses the same setter once per explicitly listed section; it never invents a new section or applies to rows the owner did not see.

Retain each acknowledgement's section primary key, ULID, resulting type, classification source and changed flag. A manual resolved type survives rescans even after changed headings or automatic inference until explicitly revoked; setting uncertain revokes the override and coherently sets uncertain confidence and review=true. The setter preserves heading, anchors, status and links. Same application is a no-op. Never call `add_plan_section` as an update or direct generic classification update, never mutate checkpoints or provider config.

##### Step 4: Report actual results

Report acknowledged ids, remaining uncertain count and reasons for unresolved/skipped rows. On partial failure keep acknowledged ids, show precisely which rows were completed and which remain; do not create replacements or blindly retry an ambiguous write response. Rerunning already-resolved sections makes no new classification write. End with the named `plan-status` progress hint.

#### Rules

- **Language.** A quoted question, option, screen or report fixes what it
  says, not its wording: write it in the language of the conversation. Keep
  unchanged: identifiers, commands, paths, file contents, commit messages,
  changelog entries, short titles and anything shown verbatim.

The common consent boundary is the exact readable proposal before the user's explicit response. A selected default, timeout, silence, unattended run, old handoff or generated proposal is never approval. Changed scope requires a fresh concrete preview; reuse unchanged explicit consent already given. A report is not a consent request. Keep every proposal word visible before acceptance; hidden thinking, truncated content and a reference to an unavailable screen do not suffice.

Use the current host's eligible consent UI when it exposes complete previews; otherwise show the full decision material in visible text and ask for the explicit reply. Workflow references to dialog previews/Details pages mean the same complete readable content, translated to the current host's supported presentation. Never depend on hidden thinking, omitted pages or a Plan-only/optional-question-only permission tool.

Discover only tools needed by the selected branch, using the current host's available discovery mechanism. Invoke tools with separate top-level parameters from their actual descriptions; illustrative `mcp__dct__` prefixes name DCT tools, not a requirement for one host's namespace. An unavailable operation is a readable capability refusal, never a reason for direct SQL or ad hoc Python writes.

Use the available MCP discovery mechanism. No client-specific discovery tool, task mirror, hooks or publisher is assumed.

No provider is silently enabled, and unresolved stays unresolved on unavailable capability. Manual and bulk choices use the same semantic setter; no direct SQL or ad hoc Python fallback.

## `/plan-status` fallback

### plan-status — Cross-plan Progress Dashboard

#### When to invoke

- User asks about progress across plans in the current project.
- Session start / handoff — show high-level plan health alongside sprint review.
- Before making planning decisions (pick a plan with most pending work, etc.).

#### Workflow

##### Step 1: Resolve project

Auto-detect from CWD via `mcp__dct__list_projects()` + longest-prefix match.
If not registered, ask via the supported decision interaction.

##### Step 2: Fetch plans

`mcp__dct__list_plans(project=<slug>, status="active")` — returns `{cols, rows}`.

##### Step 3: Enrich each plan with progress

For each plan row, call `mcp__dct__get_plan(plan_id=<integer primary key>)` to get the `progress`
sub-dict and sections needing review.

##### Step 4: Render table

```
#   kind    status  progress  uncertain  last-scanned  title
──  ──────  ──────  ────────  ─────────  ────────────  ─────────────────────
12  plan    active  8/10      2          2026-04-17    Plans/roadmaps schema
17  spec    active  3/3       0          2026-04-15    …
23  adr     active  —         0          2026-04-10    ADR-001: Use ULIDs
```

`progress` format:
- Plans with checkpoints: `done/active` (rejected excluded).
- Plans with only sections and no checkpoints (specs, ADRs): show `—`.

`uncertain`: count of `plan_sections.needs_llm_review=TRUE`.

##### Step 5: Optional drill-down

The table is the final text of the turn — a report with no decision attached,
so no dialog follows it: text written before a dialog can land in the
thinking block, which the user sees only as a one-line summary. End it with one line: "Name a plan to see its sections." When the
user names one: `mcp__dct__get_plan(id)` full dump + structured section
tree.

#### Rules

- **Language.** A quoted question, option, screen or report fixes what it
  says, not its wording: write it in the language of the conversation. Keep
  unchanged: identifiers, commands, paths, file contents, commit messages,
  changelog entries, short titles and anything shown verbatim.
- Read-only — never modify plans / sections / checkpoints from this skill.
- Respect `format="structured"` default — pretty-print only at the final
  rendering step, not in the MCP calls themselves.
- When no plans exist, emit a one-liner (`"No plans registered in <project>"`)
  and stop — do not suggest creating one unprompted.

>
>   #   kind   status  progress  uncertain  last-scanned  title
>   ── ─────  ──────  ────────  ─────────  ────────────  ─────
>   12  plan   active  6/10      0          2026-04-17    v0.2.0 implementation
>   ...
>
>   Name a plan to see its sections.

## `/release` fallback

### release — one screen, one answer

The release is EXECUTED by the local workflow — `dct release plan / prepare /
apply / resume / abandon / reconstruct / takeover / version-files / status`,
all with `--json` (schemas, order of effects, refusals:
`docs/release-workflow.md`; code: `dct/workflows/release/`). This skill runs
the DIALOG, in ONE workflow from the first plan to the pushed tag: it reads
what the workflow reports, shows the owner one screen, and passes the
owner's answer back as flags. The authoritative step list is the `release`
fallback of `docs/assistant-fallbacks.md`; this skill follows it step for
step.

A typical release uses one decision interaction carrying the complete screen. Show "Checking proj-a…" while preparing. The owner sees all version/action material and answers explicitly through the host presentation below; when no eligible UI exists, complete visible text plus the owner's explicit reply is the consent route.

Steps 0-5 are the typical path. **Rare cases** (after Step 5) and the
Resume path are read only when a step points there; the Legacy path only
when the owner asks for it.

The workflow performs and verifies every release effect and records it.
This skill therefore:
- never edits the changelog file FOR THE RELEASE (the workflow writes the
  section) and never runs the version script itself;
- never stages, commits or tags FOR THE RELEASE: the commit of the owner's
  uncommitted changes, the empty commit that marks waiting entries as done,
  the release commit and the tag are made by the workflow (`apply
  --consent`, or `resume`), through the repository's hooks;
- never calls `advance_release` and never stamps through
  `release_changelog` — an entry added or corrected during the dialog never
  takes a version (the stamp of `apply` is the only writer of versions);
- does not run a push of its own: the push is a step of `apply` / `resume`,
  to the target the screen showed;
- never resets, stashes or cleans the owner's work, and does not use the
  `clog release` alias.

Run every command in the CURRENT checkout (your shell's working directory),
never in the MCP server's directory. Add `-P <slug>` only when the project is
not detected from the CWD.

Without the CLI (an MCP-only host), a release is not possible from here: the ledger tools (`release_changelog`, `get_release`, `advance_release`) cannot verify the changelog file, version files, commit, tag or push. Report that capability refusal and the concrete CLI setup/reconnect remedy; never imitate effects with raw ledger writes.

#### Plain words

What the owner reads uses these words. Identifiers (`details` keys, ids of
digests, reasons such as `no_trailer`) appear only on the final "Technical
details" line of a message.

| internal | say |
| --- | --- |
| candidate / HEAD | your latest commit abc1234 |
| proven / stamped | goes in / released in 0.2.0 |
| `no_trailer` | not included yet — no commit says it is done |
| `reverted` / `revert_unconfirmed` | its change was undone by 0f1e2d3 / a later commit may have undone it |
| `below_range` | only linked to commits from before v0.1.0 |
| `squash_suspected` | probably came in with 'Add watcher (#42)' |
| attest | mark as done — it is already committed (report: "added an empty commit recording that") |
| `Changelog:` line | this commit marks as done: … |
| uncertain candidate | #2 Dark mode might be part of this work too |
| version-only | only the version number, no changelog entries |
| contract change | dct will update VERSION in every future release |
| version-sync script | your version script (scripts/dct-version-sync.sh — its path, `consent.version_files.script.identity`) |
| push target / no upstream | push to origin/main (url) / this branch isn't connected to a remote branch |
| range base / approximate | counting changes since v0.1.1 / no earlier release tag — commits since 12 Mar |
| record, reconstruct | report only: 0.1.0 was released before you used dct — nothing to do |
| unfinished record | release 0.2.0 isn't finished (tagged here, not pushed) |
| own executor | released with its own tool |
| busy lock (exit 1, `details.lock`) / conflict (exit 75) | another release command is running / the dct database changed at the same moment |
| digest, snapshot, consent, plan / prepare / apply | never shown |

The one phrase for coming back, everywhere: "run release again".

#### Workflow

##### Step 0: Capability probe and the plan

Run `dct release plan --json`.

- Command missing, exit 2 with `invalid choice` / an unknown argument, or a
  `schema_version` lower than 5 (no `executor`, `changelog_file`,
  `version.suggested` or `pending_consent` key — an older CLI) → STOP:
  "Your dct is missing or older than this release. Upgrade it with
  `dct upgrade` (or `uv tool upgrade dctracker`, or `pipx upgrade
  dctracker`; not installed: `uv tool install 'dctracker[mcp]'`), restart
  the current client, then run release again." Do NOT fall back to the MCP tools:
  the ledger tools alone cannot verify the changelog file, the version
  files, the commit, the tag or the push.
- Exit 1 → one plain sentence with its next step, then STOP; never retry
  from another directory. Project not found: "This folder isn't registered
  with dct yet. Register it with `dct project add <slug> .` (a short name
  of your choice), then run release again." A checkout that could not be
  verified: the next step the CLI's message names, in plain words.

##### Step 1: Route — from this ONE plan result (K-111, K-119)

The plan carries the routing, read in one transaction: `kind`,
`unfinished_release` and `executor` — `executor.project` (the project's
release-executor setting TODAY) and `executor.record` (`null`, or the
unfinished record's `version`, `status`, stored `executor`,
`progress_owner` and `consent`). Decide from this ONE result; run no other
command to find out who releases (a later read can disagree with the plan).
An unfinished release (`kind == "resume"`) is routed by what the RECORD
stores, whatever the setting says today; `executor.project` applies ONLY to
a NEW release. Never ask the owner again merely because the setting for
future releases changed; one line saying so is enough.

| the plan shows (the FIRST matching row routes) | who finishes it | path |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind == "resume"` and `executor.record.progress_owner == "dct"` | dct, on the consent STORED on the record | **Resume path** → `dct release resume` at once when the owner asked to continue (no second question) |
| `kind == "resume"` and `executor.record.executor == "own"` | the project's own release tool | **Resume path** → hand over: its tool finishes it through the ledger path; dct runs nothing and takes nothing over |
| `kind == "resume"` and `executor.record.consent == false` | nobody automatically — a `dct` record stamped outside `apply` | **Resume path** → offer `dct release takeover` (a NEW consent the owner approves) or the ledger path |
| `kind == "release"` and `executor.project == "own"` | the project's own release tool | the hand-over sentence (Rare cases), then STOP |
| `kind == "release"` and `executor.project == "dct"` | dct | Step 2 |

Every later plan of this dialog is routed by the same table. For a new
release dct runs, two more reads of the same plan, in this order (no commit
made under the owner's Release goes unmentioned; a Finish refused for the
changelog file comes back through its refusal row):

1. `pending_consent.consent_digest` set and `pending_consent.adoptable`
   true (dct made a commit under an earlier Release) → the Finish question
   (Rare cases), nothing else. `consent_digest` null but `progress` records
   a commit → "A commit made under an earlier Release" (Rare cases). No
   commit recorded → a preview without a commit is only a draft: go on —
   the next preview replaces it.
2. `changelog_file.problem` set → the changelog-file question (Rare
   cases), then plan again from Step 0. The plan checks the file as the
   preview will — against the tree the work-in-progress commit of the
   uncommitted changes will have — so a difference that commit settles (an
   uncommitted edit of the changelog, a conversion to Markdown, a link
   replaced by a file) is no problem and never asked. A problem that comes
   back after its way was taken is never asked a second time: go on to the
   preview (Step 2) — it checks the file against the commit it builds, and
   a real problem comes back as its `details.changelog_file` refusal.

##### Step 2: Before the screen — silent

Show "Checking proj-a…" and run, in this order:

1. `dct release status --version <current> --json` (only when
   `version.current` is set) — read for ONE sentence of the report (K-2);
   outcome `none` (released before dct kept records) is said there.
2. **Uncommitted changes — the work in progress** (the plan's
   `index.clean` is false — staged, unstaged or deleted paths — OR any
   `index.release_artifacts[].untracked` is true OR a new file of
   `index.untracked` is plainly part of the same work) are committed INSIDE
   the release, in this workflow: `apply --consent` commits your changes
   through the repository's hooks, as the screen shows them. Drafting that
   commit's message is your job, not a request to the owner: do not tell
   the owner to commit and come back.
   Run `dct clog candidates --json`, read the diff (`git diff HEAD`, `git
   status --porcelain=v2`) and draft the message in conventional format
   (the `commit` skill's Step 6 format): a subject with the `(v<current>)`
   suffix, then the line `Changelog: <confirmed ids that describe this
   diff>` — only `confirmed` candidates whose text matches the diff; an
   `uncertain` one never goes in (the screen says it "might be part of this
   work too"). Write it to a scratch file (your scratchpad, never the
   project); it becomes `--message-file`, for a dirty tree only (dct
   refuses a message on a clean tree). A new untracked file (the plan's
   `index.untracked`) goes in with `--include-untracked <path>` only when
   it is plainly part of the same work — then there is work to commit, also
   on an otherwise clean tree, so the message is drafted; every other one
   stays out and the screen lists it ("Not included", from the preview's
   `details.left_out`) — never a path that looks like a secret (`dct clog
   candidates --json` lists them under `secret_like`) or build output. Do
   not ask the nested commit questions (the
   version-bump redirect, "add an entry?", "track the untracked files?"):
   the screen replaces them. A merge, rebase, cherry-pick or revert in
   progress, or a conflicted path → STOP: "A merge is in progress — finish
   it (`git merge --continue`) or cancel it (`git merge --abort`), then run
   release again." (the others: their own `--continue` / `--abort`).
3. **The preview** — ONE call computes the whole release (the commit of the
   uncommitted changes, the entries, the changelog section, the version
   files, the checks, the push) on commits no branch points to, and stores
   it; nothing is committed, staged, tagged or pushed. It runs the version
   script BEFORE the owner answers, in an isolated copy that is not a
   sandbox, so the script must change only the version files and never
   wrap a release, publish or deploy command:

   ```bash
   dct release prepare --preview --json --message-file <scratch file> --include-untracked <path>   # uncommitted changes
   dct release prepare --preview --json                                                            # a clean tree
   ```

   Exit 0, outcome `preview` → Step 3 (nothing goes in and more than 4
   entries wait → first the question of Rare cases, "Before the screen").
   Otherwise test these two FIRST, before any refusal row:
   `details.version_unresolved` (a refusal, exit 1: no version can be
   suggested) → the "Which version is this release?" question, and outcome
   `failed` (the version script failed or timed out — `details.sync`; a
   failed result has no `display`) → the stop, both in Rare cases, "Before
   the screen". Only then any other refusal → "When a command refuses"
   (Rare cases).
4. **Publishing workflows** — any `.github/workflows/*.yml` or `*.yaml`
   with an `on: push: tags` trigger: pushing the tag publishes. The screen
   says so in its "Then:" block.

##### Step 3: The screen — ONE decision interaction with two questions

The screen is rendered only from this preview's `variants[shown].consent`
and its `display` (the work block from the same preview's `details.work`,
the one remote line from `details.remote`), with no other source — nothing
from the plan, nothing you computed. The version in the headline is
`variants[shown].consent.version.target`. (`variants[shown]` is the entry
of the preview's `variants` list whose `name` is `shown`; `variants[all]`
the one whose `name` is `all`.)

```
Ready to release proj-a 0.1.1 (now 0.1.0) — a patch, because it only fixes things

Your uncommitted changes are committed first:
  src/help.py, src/cli.py (all of it, including the parts you didn't stage), README.md
  Not included: notes.txt (new, not tracked by git)
  Message: "fix: correct the help text (v0.1.0)"
  This commit marks as done: #1 Typo in help
  #2 Dark mode might be part of this work too. If so, choose 'Release with all 2'.
Goes in (1):
  Fixed    Typo in help                   #1
Not included yet (1) — no commit says it is done (a commit says so with a line like 'Changelog: 2'):
  Added    Dark mode                      #2
Files:  CHANGELOG.md (new 0.1.1 section) · VERSION 0.1.0 → 0.1.1
        First release with dct: dct will update VERSION in every future release.
Counting changes since v0.1.0.
With all 2: 0.2.0 — also #2; VERSION 0.1.0 → 0.2.0
Then:   commit "release: v0.1.1", tag v0.1.1, push both to origin/main
        (git@github.com:me/proj-a.git)
        Pushing the tag starts your publish workflow (publish.yml).
```

(Fixes only → a patch; "with all 2" adds something → a minor version. On
0.x the two differ only when the shown entries are fixes only.)

The blocks, in this order (leave out a block that is empty):

- **The work block** (`details.work`, only with uncommitted changes): the
  paths — a path whose `staged` is `part` or `none` is marked "all of it,
  including the parts you didn't stage"; the "Not included" line (below);
  the message verbatim; "marks as done: …"
  (`work.proves`); each `work.uncertain` entry as "#2 Dark mode might be
  part of this work too. If so, choose 'Release with all 2'." (no "all"
  variant: "If so, say so under 'Change something'.").
- **Not included** — every entry of `details.left_out`: the new untracked
  files the release does not commit, also on a clean tree (`details.work`
  is null): "Not included: notes.txt (new, not tracked by git)"; one whose
  `secret_like` is true: "Not included: .env (looks like a secret — left
  out on purpose)" — never included or offered. The dialog stages nothing
  itself; a file goes in only through `--include-untracked`.
- **The empty commit** — only when `variants[shown].consent.attest` is not
  null: "First an empty commit records that #2 is already done.", first in
  "Then:".
- **What goes in and what waits** — `display.entries.selected` and
  `display.entries.waiting`, each waiting reason in plain words (a reverted
  one: "its change was undone by 0f1e2d3"); the first waiting heading
  carries once "(a commit says so with a line like 'Changelog: 2')".
  Nothing selected → "No changelog entries — only the version number
  changes", and above the list ONE sentence: "None of your commits is
  linked to these entries yet (a commit links one with a line like
  'Changelog: 3'). If the work is already committed, choose 'Release with
  all 3': dct adds an empty commit recording that." (no "all" variant: "…
  tell me which ones under 'Change something'."). Outside git: "Goes in
  (4) — not checked against commits (this project isn't in git)".
- **Files and checks** — `display.checks` ("VERSION 0.1.0 → 0.2.0", "+N
  lines with 0.2.0"); the section is `display.section`; the contract line
  ("dct will update VERSION in every future release") only when its
  `change` is true (`display.contract`). `consent.version_files.script`
  null → "No version file changes — dct changes them only through
  scripts/dct-version-sync.sh, which proj-a doesn't have." Script output →
  "Your version script (scripts/dct-version-sync.sh) printed 14 lines —
  say 'show details'" (`display.sync`).
- **The range line** — `display.range.text`, plus `display.range.notice`
  when set; answering Release confirms it, it is never asked again.
  `display.range.approximate` → "No earlier release tag — looking at
  commits since 12 Mar".
- **The "with all N" line** — `display.delta` of the "all" variant.
- **"Then:"** — `consent.push`: `mode` `push` → the commit, the tag
  `push.tag`, and where (`push.remote`/`push.branch`, `push.url`); the
  publishing workflow, when Step 2 found one. `mode` `local` → "not
  pushed: <reason>" — `requested` "you asked not to push", `no_upstream`
  "this branch isn't connected to a remote branch", `upstream_invalid`
  "this branch's remote branch can't be pushed to", `detached` "you are not
  on a branch", `several_urls` "origin pushes to 2 places and dct pushes to
  one — pick one under Change something", `url_not_literal` "git would
  rewrite origin's push address". `mode` `push` with
  `details.remote.checked` false (the remote could not be read during the
  preview) adds one line: "origin could not be reached now — it is checked
  again when you release."
- Every `display.warnings` line, in plain words. The shown variant's
  `suggested.safe` false → the headline says why, keyed on its
  `suggested.reason`: `tag_taken` "v0.2.0 already exists — releasing
  0.2.1"; `breaking` "a major version, because something was removed";
  `after_tag` "no version is recorded yet, so it counts on from the tag
  v0.1.0".

Then ONE decision interaction with two questions. Every version a label names
is the `consent.version.target` of the variant that label applies — never
`suggested.target`, which differs after an explicit `--version`:
V_shown = `variants[shown].consent.version.target`, V_all =
`variants[all].consent.version.target`.

**Q1 — the action.** Question, without a version (the version question
picks it): "Release proj-a and push it to origin/main?" ("Release proj-a
here, without pushing?" for `push.mode == "local"`; after "None" in the
more-than-4 question: "Release only the version number?"). Options, in
this order:

1. "Release" — "Commit, tag and push to origin/main. The version you pick
   can't be released again." The label follows the shown variant, and IS
   that consent: "Release locally (no push)" when `push.mode == "local"`;
   "Release (version only)" when `version_only` is true, described "Only
   the version number changes; the changelog gets no new section, and this
   version won't appear in the exported changelog."
2. "Release with all N" — only when the preview made the "all" variant
   (`all_unavailable` is null); never first. dct makes it only when 1 to 4
   entries wait and none of them is reverted — never for reverted entries
   or more than 4 waiting; you never build this option yourself. Its
   description: "Only if the work for #2 is already committed. dct records
   that with an empty commit, then releases." When V_all differs from
   V_shown the label names it: "Release with all 2 as 0.2.0".
3. "Change something" — "Which entries, where it is pushed, edit an
   entry — or 'show details'." For `first_version` (it has no version
   question): "Another version, which entries, where it is pushed, edit an
   entry — or 'show details'."
4. "Stop" — "Nothing is released; nothing in your project changes." After
   a commit was made (`details.made` of the refusal that led here): "Stop
   — nothing is released; your changes stay committed as abc1234."

The screen is in Q1's previews: "Release" (in each of its forms) carries the
screen of the shown variant, "Release with all N" the screen of the "all"
variant, "Change something" one line per thing it can change, "Stop" what
stays as it is. A screen longer than 15 lines: the option's preview is a
summary page — the headline, one line per block with its count ("Goes in: 25
entries — on the Details pages") and the "Then:" lines — and the whole
screen, in order, is on the pages of one more single-select question,
"Details" (after Q2; for a first version, after Q1), each page at most 15
lines; its answer is not a decision.

**Q2 — the version.** Question: "Which version?" Options:

- Keep, listed first and marked recommended, built from V_shown: "Keep
  0.1.1 (recommended)". When the "all" variant exists and V_all differs,
  the label names both: "Keep the suggested version: 0.1.1, or 0.2.0 with
  all 2 (recommended)". On a screen after the owner typed another version,
  V_shown IS that version: "Keep 0.3.0 (your choice)".
- then the `suggested.alternatives` with what each means ("0.2.0 —
  something new"), leaving out only V_shown; when V_all differs it stays
  in the list for the shown entries alone: "0.2.0 — without #2";
- then Other to type a version.

Q2 is omitted for `first_version` (`suggested.reason`: no version and no
release tag yet): the headline shows the proposed version, "Ready to
release proj-a 0.1.0 — its first release", and the dialog is the action
question alone. The version is proposed by dct and approved by the owner
with Release: Q2 changes it, and for `first_version` (no Q2) "Change
something" does.

There is NO "include without proof" option: an entry goes in only when a commit says it is done — the work commit's `Changelog:` line or the empty commit of "Release with all N".

##### Step 4: After the answer

| answer | what runs |
| --- | --- |
| "Release" + "Keep" | `dct release apply --consent <variants[shown].consent_digest> --confirm --json`, then Step 5 — no other question |
| "Release with all N" + "Keep" | `dct release apply --consent <variants[all].consent_digest> --confirm --json`, then Step 5 |
| "Release" + another version V2 | `dct release prepare --preview --version <V2> --json` with every earlier flag — the same message file, untracked files, `--attest`, `--entries` / `--no-entries` and push flags as before; then the screen again, headed "Version changed to 0.3.0" |
| "Release with all N" + another version V2 | the "all" variant's selection REPLACES the earlier one: drop every earlier `--entries`, `--no-entries` and `--attest`, then `dct release prepare --preview --version <V2> --entries <variants[all].consent.entries.selected> --attest <variants[all].consent.attest.ids> --json` — the message file, untracked files and push flags stay as before — so that the new screen's first option IS the release with all N; then the screen again, headed "Version changed to 0.3.0" |
| "Change something" + any version | Dialog B (Rare cases), then `update_changelog` / `delete_changelog` for edits, then the preview again with every earlier flag plus the changed ones (a push choice replaces the earlier push flags — Dialog B; another version in Q2 → also `--version <V2>`; another first version typed in Dialog B → `--version <V>`); then the screen again |
| "Stop" + any version | `dct release prepare --discard-preview --json`. Nothing else. |

A first version has no Q2 (`first_version`): its answers read as + "Keep"
— "Release" applies `variants[shown].consent_digest`, the version the
screen showed.

Never pass a digest the screen did not show: `apply --consent` only with the consent_digest of the variant whose content the screen rendered. The one exception is the Finish question (Rare cases): it passes `pending_consent.consent_digest`, the screen the owner already said Release to.

A refusal (exit 1 `refused`, exit 75 `conflict`) → "When a command
refuses" (Rare cases).

##### Step 5: Read the result and report

- Exit 0, outcome `completed` → the report (below). Outcome `noop` → the
  version is already released, nothing was done; a warning naming
  `dct release reconstruct` becomes one report sentence (the **Legacy
  path** runs only when the owner asks for it).
- Exit 1, outcome `refused` → "When a command refuses" (Rare cases); only
  the listed `steps` happened, and a release that is now unfinished
  continues on the **Resume path**, on the stored consent, once the cause
  is gone.
- Every `warnings` line of a result, also of a successful one, in plain
  words — a post-commit hook that failed after the commit was published
  (the release stands), a pin or stored blob that could not be cleaned.

The report is plain text; identifiers go only on the final "Technical
details" line. Report the requested version (`details.requested_version`),
the record's `version` (the authoritative spelling of every artifact) and
the project's `details.current_version` SEPARATELY (K-55 / K-31), on that
line:

```
Released proj-a 0.2.0 — commit and tag v0.2.0 pushed to origin/main.
  In it: #3, #4. Waiting for a later release: #1, #2 (no commit says they are done).
  Your changes were committed first as 4b5c6d7; #2 was marked as done with an empty commit.
  0.1.0 was released before you used dct — nothing to do.
  Pushing the tag started your publish workflow.
Technical details: requested 0.2.0 · record 0.2.0 · current_version 0.2.0 · commit abc1234 · steps work_commit attest stamp changelog version_files commit index tag push complete done · push url git@github.com:me/proj-a.git
```

A local release: "Released proj-a 0.2.0 here — commit and tag v0.2.0, not
pushed (you can push the tag yourself later)." The missing older record is
that one short sentence; "record 0.1.0" (the **Legacy path**) is mentioned
only when the owner asks about that version's history.

#### Rare cases

Read a part of this section, and the Resume path after it, only when a step
above points there. Wherever this section, the Resume path or the Legacy path
(reached only when the owner asks for it) says to show something and then ask, what is shown is the preview of the
option it belongs to (pages when longer than 15 lines — Rules); something
shown with no question after it is the final text of the turn.

##### A project released with its own tool

dct's `prepare` / `apply` / `resume` refuse a new release of an `own`
project before any write (`details.executor`). Say ONE sentence and STOP:
"proj-a is released with its own tool, not by dct. Ready for it: #3, #4;
waiting: #1, #2. Run that tool; it records the release in dct." (the ids
from the plan's `entries.proven` and `entries.unproven`). Its tool follows
`docs/release-workflow.md#integrating-a-projects-own-release-tool`: it
stamps through the ledger with `expected_executor="own"` and reports each
verified effect, the tag with its `tag_proof`. Never run a command stored
anywhere in its place. A release its tool made before release records
existed is recorded by the **Legacy path** (the `--evidence` row) only when
the owner asks for it.

##### The Finish question — a release the owner already approved

`pending_consent.consent_digest` is set (it is null until the owner said
Release and dct made a commit under that answer) and
`pending_consent.adoptable` is true → ask ONE question, nothing else. Its
text says what is released, from `pending_consent.applied` (the variant the
owner said Release to: `version`, `entries`, `attest`) and
`pending_consent.progress`: "You said Release for proj-a 0.2.0 (#3, #4) and
dct committed your changes as abc1234, but the release didn't finish."
(only `progress.attest_commit` recorded: "… and dct marked #1, #2 as done
in abc1234, but …" — the ids of `applied.attest`). When `applied.attest`
is not empty and `progress.attest_commit` is null, add: "Finishing also
adds the empty commit that marks #1, #2 as done." Options: "Finish
releasing 0.2.0" / "Stop — nothing is released; abc1234 stays on your
branch". Finish runs the same answer again — dct adopts the commit it made
and makes no second one — then Step 5:

```bash
dct release apply --consent <pending_consent.consent_digest> --confirm --json
```

Stop runs `dct release prepare --discard-preview --json` exactly like the
screen's Stop; the commit stays.

##### A commit made under an earlier Release

`consent_digest` null but `progress` records a commit (`work_commit` or
`attest_commit`): a commit was made under an earlier Release, and that
release cannot be finished here. `pending_consent.blocked` says why
(`blocked.why`) and the step that works instead (`blocked.next_step`).
By `blocked.why`:

- `other_checkout` (`pending_consent.checkout_root` is not this checkout)
  → ONE sentence and STOP: "The release you approved earlier was started
  in <checkout_root> — run release again in that folder."
- `branch_switched` (HEAD is on another branch than at the preview, or
  detached where a branch was, or the reverse) → ONE sentence,
  `blocked.next_step` in plain words with the command it names exactly as
  written, and STOP. It is never a new preview on the switched branch: that would replace the
  release the owner approved and leave its commit behind. The owner takes
  that step and runs release again (→ the Finish question); only when the
  owner says to release from this branch instead does the dialog go on to
  the new preview below.
- `head_moved` / `progress_lost` → `blocked.next_step` IS a new preview:
  ONE line before it, chosen by what still exists, with every plan
  `warnings` line that names the commit:
  - a recorded commit the plan's `warnings` say no longer exists (reset
    away, pruned) → "The commit dct made for your earlier release
    (abc1234) is gone — here is the release again." (uncommitted changes
    need a drafted message again, Step 2);
  - only `attest_commit` recorded → "#1, #2 were already marked as done in
    abc1234; the release you approved earlier didn't finish, so here it is
    again.";
  - a `work_commit` that still exists → "Your changes are already
    committed as abc1234; the release you approved earlier didn't finish,
    so here it is again."

##### Previewing again after a commit was made

A new preview that follows a commit dct already made (a refusal of apply,
the Finish question refused, or the line above):

- in this conversation it keeps every earlier flag; after a Finish, or in a
  new conversation, there are none — take them from
  `pending_consent.applied`: `--version <applied.version>`, `--entries
  <applied.entries>` (`applied.entries` empty → `--no-entries`: an empty
  `--entries` is refused, and leaving the flag out would select every
  proven entry — another release than the one the owner approved),
  `--attest <applied.attest>` when not empty. The push
  target is not recorded, so the screen shows the default one: say once
  "Check where it is pushed — it was set again.";
- drop the `--attest` ids a made `attest_commit` already marks (they are
  proven now; passing them again is refused);
- pass a newly drafted `--message-file` whenever the plan shows uncommitted
  changes — also after a commit was made (never on a clean tree);
- the screen names what `made` holds, and its Stop reads "Stop — nothing is
  released; your changes stay committed as abc1234".

##### Change something — Dialog B

Discover `update_changelog` and `delete_changelog` only when an entry change needs them.

Discover only tools needed by the selected branch, using the current host's available discovery mechanism. Invoke tools with separate top-level parameters from their actual descriptions; illustrative `mcp__dct__` prefixes name DCT tools, not a requirement for one host's namespace. An unavailable operation is a readable capability refusal, never a reason for direct SQL or ad hoc Python writes.

Use the available MCP discovery mechanism. No client-specific discovery tool, task mirror, hooks or publisher is assumed.
Then ONE decision interaction with at most 4 questions; a question that does not
apply is left out, and each one's first option keeps what the screen
showed:

1. "Which waiting entries are already committed?" (multiSelect) — one
   option per waiting entry: "#2 Dark mode — only if already committed";
   "#16, #17 — probably came in with 'Add watcher (#42)'". More than 4
   waiting: "All waiting", or Other to type ids. A reverted entry is not
   offered. → `--attest <ids>`.
2. "Which entries go in?" (multiSelect over what goes in), with "None —
   release only the version number" (that label is the version-only
   consent). The decision interaction interface takes at most 4 options: more than 3 entries
   go in → "Keep all" and "None — release only the version number", the
   question text lists every entry with its id, and Other to type the ids
   that go in. → `--entries <ids>`, or `--no-entries`.
3. "Where is it pushed?" — keyed on the shown variant's
   `consent.push.mode`, never on a target the screen did not show.
   `push.mode` `push` → "Keep <remote>/<branch>" (from
   `consent.push.remote`/`consent.push.branch`), "Don't push — keep it on
   this computer", one option per other push address of that remote (`git
   remote get-url --push --all <remote>`, read-only); Other: a remote and a
   branch. `push.mode` `local` → "Keep it on this computer", then one
   option per configured remote (`git remote`, read-only) with the branch
   the preview read, `details.base.branch`: "Push to <remote>/<branch>" (a
   detached HEAD has no branch: Other only); for the reason `several_urls`
   instead one option per push address of the branch's remote (`git config
   branch.<branch>.remote`, then `git remote get-url --push --all
   <remote>`, read-only); Other: a remote and a branch. At most 4 options:
   more than 2 other push addresses → only the first two options, the
   question text lists the other addresses (and the remotes that do not
   fit), and Other takes one of them (typed as listed) or a remote and a
   branch.
   → `--push-remote <remote> --push-branch <branch>` only — the
   preview derives and checks the address, and the screen again shows it;
   `--push-url <url>` is added only for an address the owner picked from
   that `git remote get-url --push --all` list, never one you derived
   (a fetch URL can differ from the push URL). Or `--no-push`. The owner
   picks ONE address; there is no mirror mode.
   The push choice REPLACES every earlier push flag (`--no-push`,
   `--push-remote`, `--push-branch`, `--push-url`) instead of adding to
   them: dct refuses `--no-push` beside a push target. So a push target
   drops `--no-push`; "Don't push" / "Keep it on this computer" drops every
   `--push-remote`, `--push-branch` and `--push-url`; another remote or
   address drops the earlier `--push-url` (it named the old address).
   "Keep <remote>/<branch>" changes nothing.
4. "Anything else? To edit or delete an entry, type 'edit #2: new text' or
   'delete #2' under Other." (for `first_version` it adds: "To release
   another first version, type 'version 0.5.0'.") — "Nothing else", "Also
   commit notes.txt" (only for a file of `details.left_out` whose
   `secret_like` is false — a secret-looking one is never offered), "Show
   details" (the section, the
   version script's output, each entry's proof — a PR number WITH its
   origin, `pr_source`: `git` = recognised in the repository; `client` =
   declared by a client, never presented as git's recognition — on the
   "Details" pages of the screen's dialog, asked again); Other: "edit #2: <new text>" →
   `mcp__dct__update_changelog`, "delete #2" (gone for good) →
   `mcp__dct__delete_changelog`, and for `first_version` only (it has no
   Q2) "version <V>" → `--version <V>` on the next preview.

Then preview again — every earlier flag plus the changed ones (where it is
pushed: by the rule above):

```bash
dct release prepare --preview --attest <ids> --json
dct release prepare --preview --entries <ids> --json
dct release prepare --preview --no-entries --json
dct release prepare --preview --push-remote <remote> --push-branch <branch> --json
dct release prepare --preview --push-remote <remote> --push-branch <branch> --push-url <the address the owner picked> --json
dct release prepare --preview --no-push --json
dct release prepare --preview --include-untracked <path> --message-file <scratch file> --json
```

Version files cannot be changed here. One line says: "The file changes
come from your version script (scripts/dct-version-sync.sh) — fix it,
commit it, then run release again." (no version script: "dct changes
version files only through scripts/dct-version-sync.sh — add one that
takes the version as its argument and changes only the version files,
commit it, then run release again.")

##### The changelog file

`changelog_file.problem` set — prepare and apply refuse it before the
stamp, so it is settled before the preview, with ONE question built from
`changelog_file.found` and its `ways` (each `what` and `command`). Then
plan again from Step 0. By problem:

- `ambiguous` (several Markdown changelogs) → one option per offered
  `changelog-path` way (`"Use CHANGES.md"`; a link among them is offered as
  the path through its target) — run its `dct project changelog-path
  <slug> <path>`; a link without an admissible target is not a choice: its
  "Replace the link" way and "Turn dct's changelog file off" are (K-27);
- `case_variant` (the stored path differs from a tracked file only in
  case) → "Use <found>" (its `changelog-path` command) / "Stop";
- `not_markdown` (the only changelog is not Markdown, e.g. `HISTORY.rst`,
  or the stored path has no Markdown extension) → its ways: "Convert it to
  Markdown" (you rewrite its content in the Keep a Changelog layout AND
  rename it to a Markdown extension, e.g. `git mv HISTORY.rst HISTORY.md`
  — git mv alone does not convert the format —, then `dct project
  changelog-path <slug> HISTORY.md` chooses it; the change stays
  uncommitted and the screen's commit of uncommitted changes commits it;
  outside git: renamed with `mv`, nothing to commit), "Explicit Markdown
  file" (`dct project changelog-path <slug> CHANGELOG.md` — any Markdown
  name, `changelog.md` too; the old file stays as it is), "Turn dct's
  changelog file off" (`dct project changelog <slug> off`);
- `symlink` (the changelog file or a directory of its path — `component` —
  is a symbolic link; dct never writes through one) → "Use <target>" (its
  `changelog-path` command, offered only when the path through the target
  is admissible) / "Replace the link" (committed by the screen; outside git
  nothing to commit) / "Turn dct's changelog file off"; with `baseline:
  "work_tree"` the link exists only on disk (ignored / untracked) → the
  owner moves it away;
- `not_a_directory` / `not_a_file` / `outside_project` → its ways: another
  path (`dct project changelog-path <slug> <path>`), detection (`--detect`,
  offered only when the detected file also passes the work-tree check) or
  the changelog file off; `not_a_file` with `baseline: "work_tree"` = a
  TRACKED directory whose name differs only in case, opened at the path by
  a case-insensitive file system — never moved away: another path or off
  (K-28);
- `not_baseline` → by `baseline`: `absent` / `tracked` (a file at the path
  that is not the commit's content — ignored, untracked or a case-variant)
  → the owner moves it away (never an uncommitted edit of the tracked file:
  the plan checks that against the work-in-progress commit, which settles
  it); `unfiltered` (the content IS the commit's, but
  not in the form a checkout through its filters writes) → nothing to
  commit: the file is checked out again through its filters (`git rm
  --cached -q -- <path>`, then `git checkout HEAD -- <path>`).

##### Before the screen: the version, the script, many waiting entries

- `details.version_unresolved` (a refusal: the current version cannot be
  read, or every nearby version is taken) → ask ONE question, "Which
  version is this release?" (Other: type it), then preview again with
  `--version <V>`.
- Outcome `failed` (the version script failed or timed out, exit code 124)
  → STOP: "Your version script (scripts/dct-version-sync.sh) failed (exit
  1). It runs in a clean copy of your last commit (no .venv, node_modules
  or untracked tools). Last lines: … Fix it, commit it, then run release
  again. Nothing was released." (the last lines from `details.sync` — a
  failed result has no `display` —, with `output_dropped_bytes` when output
  was cut, and the environment the script ran under,
  `details.environment`, under Technical details).
- **Nothing proven with more than 4 waiting entries** — keyed on the
  waiting entries themselves, whatever `all_unavailable` says (it reads
  `reverted` before `too_many`): `display.entries.selected` of the shown
  variant is empty and `display.entries.waiting` holds more than 4 entries
  that are not reverted (no `reverted_by`, reason not `reverted` /
  `revert_unconfirmed`). Ask ONE single-select question first, "Which of
  these are already in your commits?" — the question text lists every such
  entry with its id and text; options "All of them", "None — release only
  the version number" and "Stop"; Other: type the ids. A reverted entry is
  not in the list (it waits until a commit says it is done again). "All of
  them" or typed ids → preview again with every earlier flag and `--attest
  <those ids>`, then the screen. "None" → the screen of the SAME preview
  (it already releases only the version number), its Q1 question reading
  "Release only the version number?". "Stop" — also "stop" typed under
  Other, or the question dismissed — →
  `dct release prepare --discard-preview --json`, exactly like the
  screen's Stop.

##### When a command refuses

Every refusal is one plain sentence with a true next step; `details` only
under "Technical details". Find its row in this order: first the four
bullets below (in their order), then the table of preview and apply
refusals, then the table of the release's own refusals. A bullet or a row
matches when the refusal carries one of its keys (a row: of its first
column) and every condition it states holds (WITH / without, before /
after the stamp); the first match wins — each table lists its most
specific rows first. Nothing matches → the CLI's message in plain words,
and stop.

One rule for every sentence: every refusal of apply carries
`details.made`; when `details.made` holds a commit, the sentence names it
— "your changes are already committed as abc1234" (`made.work_commit`), or
"#1, #2 were marked as done in abc1234" (only `made.attest_commit`) — and
never says "nothing was changed"; the error text "commit made, release not
started" means exactly that: say that the changes are committed as abc1234
and nothing was released. A refusal of the preview that follows such a
commit names it the same way.

- **Something moved** — `base_moved`, `work_changed`, `index_changed`,
  `hook_changed_tree`, `consent_mismatch`, `preview_replaced`,
  `date_changed` (or `missing_blobs`) — between the screen and the
  release. Run `dct release prepare --preview` again (with every earlier
  flag and the same message file while nothing was made — drafted again
  when the uncommitted changes themselves changed; after a commit:
  "Previewing again after a commit was made"), then show the screen again
  headed "Something changed since you said Release: <what, in the words of
  the table below>", and name what `made` holds ("Your changes are already
  committed as abc1234."). Never apply again silently: the owner answers
  the new screen. Example: "Something changed since you said Release: your
  pre-commit hook reformatted src/cli.py. Your changes are already
  committed as abc1234. Here is the release again." One exception: a
  `base_moved` whose `why` is `branch_switched` after a commit was made
  (`made`) is not previewed again here — plan again (`dct release plan
  --json`) and follow its `pending_consent.blocked` ("A commit made under
  an earlier Release"), never a new preview on the switched branch.
- **The one automatic re-run** — only BEFORE the stamp (the refusal has no
  `release` record and no `stamp` among its `steps`): a database conflict
  (exit 75, outcome `conflict`) or a network error, `details.git_error`
  with `details.url` and none of `hook`, `rewrite_rule`, `remote_name`
  (the push destination could not be read) → ONE automatic re-run of the
  same `apply --consent` (dct adopts what the first run made, so it is
  safe); fails again → a plain sentence and stop: "origin could not be
  reached — nothing was released (your changes are committed as
  abc1234)." That one re-run is the only retry the dialog makes on its
  own: a busy lock (exit 1) is not re-run, and every row below that says
  "the same command again" waits for the owner to say the cause is gone
  ("run release again" — which leads to the Finish question when a commit
  was made).
- **The same network error AFTER the stamp** (the refusal carries the
  `release` record, status `tagged`: commit and tag exist here) → never
  re-run apply and never say "nothing was released": "Release 0.2.0 is
  half-done: commit and tag made here; origin could not be reached. When
  the network is back, say 'finish the release'." → then the Resume path.
- **A hook rejects the commit** (`details.hook`, BEFORE the stamp: no
  `release` record) → Stop with the hook's output: "Your pre-commit hook
  stopped the commit: <its output>. Fix that, then run release again." —
  with `made` set, add "(your changes are already committed as abc1234)".
  Never `--no-verify`. A hook that changed files is `hook_changed_tree`
  above ("Your pre-commit hook changed: …"). A commit stopped for another
  cause (signing, a moved branch, the commit identity), and every one
  after the stamp: the release table's commit row, its sentence for that
  cause.

What changed, in plain words — the keys of `consent_mismatch.changed` (and
the other refusals of the list above):

| key | say |
| --- | --- |
| `work` | your uncommitted changes |
| `candidate_tree` | the files of the release |
| `attest` | which entries are marked as done |
| `entries` | the changelog entries |
| `changelog` | the changelog section |
| `version_files` | the version files |
| `version` | the version |
| `push` | where it is pushed |
| `base` | your latest commit |
| `range` | which commits are counted |
| `project`, `project_root`, `checkout_root`, `executor`, `release_mode`, `format` | where and how proj-a is released |
| `base_moved` | your branch moved (another commit, or another branch) |
| `work_changed`, `index_changed` | your files changed |
| `hook_changed_tree` | your pre-commit hook changed <paths> |
| `preview_replaced` | a newer release screen was made meanwhile |
| `date_changed`, `missing_blobs` | the date (it is past midnight UTC) / files dct had kept for the release are gone |

Preview and apply refusals, in plain words — one row per key:

| refusal | say (one plain sentence) | then |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `in_progress`, `conflicted` | "A merge is in progress — finish it (`git merge --continue`) or cancel it (`git merge --abort`), then run release again." (a rebase, cherry-pick or revert: its own `--continue` / `--abort`) | stop |
| `intent_to_add` | "notes.txt is marked to be added, but git has no content for it yet. Commit it with commit, or unmark it (`git rm --cached notes.txt`), then run release again." | stop |
| `hidden_index_flags` | "git is told to ignore changes to config.yml. Run `git update-index --no-skip-worktree config.yml` (or `--no-assume-unchanged`), then run release again." | stop |
| `submodule`, `filtered_paths` | "dct can't commit these changes for you: <path> is <a changed submodule / stored through a filter such as LFS>. Commit them with commit, then run release again." | stop |
| `secret_like` | a TRACKED path (not in the plan's `index.untracked`): "<path> looks like a secret, so dct won't commit it for you, and commit won't either. If it belongs in the repository, commit it yourself with git; otherwise stop tracking it (`git rm --cached -- <path>` and add it to .gitignore), or throw your edit away (`git restore --staged --worktree -- <path>`). Then run release again."; an untracked one: "<path> looks like a secret, so dct won't commit it. Move it out of the repository or add it to .gitignore, then run release again." | stop |
| `bad_untracked` | (yours: an untracked path you named is tracked, ignored, missing or outside) | drop it, preview again |
| `index_only` | "<paths> differ from your last commit only in what is staged — the files themselves are unchanged, so there is nothing to commit. Unstage them (`git restore --staged -- <paths>`) or make the change you meant, then run release again." (the paths from `details.index_only.paths`; the dialog never unstages for the owner) | stop |
| `message_required`, `nothing_to_commit`, `message_empty`, `message_file`, `message_foreign_ids` | (yours: the message file does not fit the tree) | fix the draft, preview again |
| `not_unproven`, `not_attestable`, `no_git` | (yours: an id that cannot be marked or selected; a selected entry without proof, `unproven`, is the release table's row) | drop it, preview again |
| `attest_without_entries` | (yours: `--attest` beside `--no-entries` — marking entries as done that nothing releases) | drop `--no-entries` (the "Release with all N" row of Step 4 replaces the selection), preview again |
| `remote_ahead` | "origin/main has commits you don't have. Run `git pull` (if git says your local changes would be overwritten, save them first with commit), then run release again." — after a commit was made, add "(your changes are already committed as abc1234)" | stop |
| `remote_tag_exists` | "v0.3.0 already exists on origin. Pick another version." | the previous screen again IN FULL (its preview is still the stored one — a refused preview stores nothing), this sentence opening its question text; no previous screen (the version came from "Which version is this release?") → that question again, this sentence opening its question text |
| `version_lower`, `version_taken`, `version_invalid` | `version_lower` (`version`, `current`): "0.1.0 is lower than the current version 0.2.0. Pick another version."; `version_taken` (`version`, `status`): "0.2.0 was already released. Pick another version." (status `abandoned`: "0.2.0 was used by a release that was abandoned. Pick another version."); `version_invalid` (`version`): "1.x isn't a version — use numbers like 1.2.3.
