Sprint membership (NOT via update_item):
- "add to sprint" / "flag for sprint" / "na sprint" / "dodaj do sprintu" →
  `mcp__dct__add_item_to_current_sprint(item_id, project)` — auto-creates the
  current sprint; additive, keeps existing members.
- "remove from sprint" / "out of sprint" / "zdejmij ze sprintu" →
  `mcp__dct__remove_item_from_current_sprint(item_id, project)`.
- To replace the WHOLE current sprint at once: `mcp__dct__set_sprint(project, item_ids)`.

#### Step 3: Execute — no confirmation question

An unambiguous instruction ("#42 to P1", "start working on #42", "w toku: 7,
12, 19") is applied without a confirmation question: call
`mcp__dct__update_item(item_id, ..., reason="…")` at once (a batch: once per id
with the same fields). Ask only when the change itself is unclear (which
field, which value). The one-line acknowledgement shows old → new, so a wrong
change is visible and reversible at once.

##### The reason travels with the update

When the transition is one of these, pass its reason IN the update call —
`mcp__dct__update_item(item_id, status=…, priority=…, reason="…")`:
- **status** change (to `in_progress`, or back to `open`) — the reason / link
  to commit; a close carries its reason as the `resolution` of `resolve_item`
- **priority** change — what prompted the bump or demotion
- **resolution** set — the commit hash or decision rationale

`reason` becomes an item note written in the SAME transaction as the
update: one operation, and a refused update (a refused tag, an invalid
status) leaves no orphan note behind. This is the audit trail — future
pickup reads these notes via `get_item`.

Title, short_title, component, description, tags edits — a reason is
welcome but not required. A note WITHOUT a field change (e.g. "pause" that
keeps the status) stays `mcp__dct__add_note(item_id, note)`.

##### Editing tags

`update_item(item_id, tags=[...])` is a **FULL REPLACE** of the item's tag set,
not an append: omit `tags` to leave it untouched, pass `[]` to clear it. To add
one tag, read the current set with `get_item(id)` first and send the union.

Tags are dictionary-backed and global: names are normalized (trimmed,
lowercased) and unknown ones auto-register, but a name too SIMILAR to an
existing tag is refused with a suggestion in the error (e.g. `test` vs `tests`).
Reuse the suggested tag, or — when the near-duplicate is genuinely wanted — call
`mcp__dct__add_tag(name=..., force=true)` first and retry the update.

For sprint membership changes, call `add_item_to_current_sprint` /
`remove_item_from_current_sprint` (or `set_sprint` for a full replace) — NOT
`update_item`.

#### Step 4: Starting work — propose the plan when the work needs one

When the update starts work on an item (status → `in_progress`: "start
working on #N", "wip"), look at its checkpoints and its description in the
`get_item` result. An item that already has checkpoints keeps its plan: name
the next pending one and add nothing.

When work starts on a non-trivial feature or improvement — or when the user
asks to break the work down — propose a plan of at least 3 checkpoints:
concrete, actionable steps, as many as the work needs (3 is a minimum, never
a cap), written at once with `mcp__dct__add_checkpoint(item_id, text)`
(remember each id) and listed under the acknowledgement. The user adjusts it
in plain words: `mcp__dct__reject_checkpoint(id)` drops a step the user
removes (ledger-kept), `add_checkpoint` adds one.

A small bug or a one-line fix starts with no checkpoints: name the next step
in the acknowledgement instead of writing an artificial plan. A complex issue
or todo may get checkpoints when its work has several real steps, with no
fixed minimum taken from its type.

#### Step 5: Acknowledge in one line

```
✓ #42 priority P2 → P1 · status open → in_progress · to undo: track-update #42 priority P2, open
```

One line per update: what changed, old → new — and it ENDS with how to undo
it, in words the user can type back; never left out, the write had no
question. To correct a wrong change, run `track-update` again with the
previous value (`update_item`). A batch is one line too:

```
✓ #7, #12, #19 status open → in_progress · to undo: track-update #7 #12 #19 open
```

#### Rules

- **Language.** A quoted question, option, screen or report fixes what it
  says, not its wording: write it in the language of the conversation. Keep
  unchanged: identifiers, commands, paths, file contents, commit messages,
  changelog entries, short titles and anything shown verbatim.
- **Every status/priority change carries a reason** (`update_item(…, reason="…")`) — no "I'll explain later" allowed.
- **No confirmation question on an unambiguous instruction** — update, then
  acknowledge in one line (old → new). A batch is one update, not one question per item.
- **ID normalization is uniform** — use the same regex as track-resolve and track-list.
- **Terminal transitions clear the DERIVED flag, not the membership** — a
  resolved / wont_fix item drops out of `in_current_sprint`, but its
  `item_sprints` link STAYS as the sprint's completion history (it is what
  `sprint_completion` counts). Sprint membership is never set via
  `update_item` — `in_current_sprint` is derived and read-only; use
  `assign_item_to_sprint` / `remove_item_from_sprint` for real membership.


The common consent boundary is the exact readable proposal before the user's explicit response. A selected default, timeout, silence, unattended run, old handoff or generated proposal is never approval. Changed scope requires a fresh concrete preview; reuse unchanged explicit consent already given. A report is not a consent request. Keep every proposal word visible before acceptance; hidden thinking, truncated content and a reference to an unavailable screen do not suffice.

Use the current host's eligible consent UI when it exposes complete previews; otherwise show the full decision material in visible text and ask for the explicit reply. Workflow references to dialog previews/Details pages mean the same complete readable content, translated to the current host's supported presentation. Never depend on hidden thinking, omitted pages or a Plan-only/optional-question-only permission tool.


Discover only tools needed by the selected branch, using the current host's available discovery mechanism. Invoke tools with separate top-level parameters from their actual descriptions; illustrative `mcp__dct__` prefixes name DCT tools, not a requirement for one host's namespace. An unavailable operation is a readable capability refusal, never a reason for direct SQL or ad hoc Python writes.

Use the available MCP discovery mechanism. No client-specific discovery tool, task mirror, hooks or publisher is assumed.

## `/triage` fallback

### triage — Review findings through the ledger

The ledger is the single source of a triage: findings are recorded right
after the review is consolidated, every version of the page is DERIVED from
`export_triage` by `dct triage page`, an agent's prefill goes in through
`suggest_findings`, the owner's answers through `decide_findings_from_text` /
`accept_suggestions`, and the closed page is derived from `close_triage`.
Nobody edits a page file by hand, and nobody hand-writes its `CARDS`,
`SUGGESTED` or `CLOSED`.

#### Tool discovery

Discover only tools needed by the selected branch, using the current host's available discovery mechanism. Invoke tools with separate top-level parameters from their actual descriptions; illustrative `mcp__dct__` prefixes name DCT tools, not a requirement for one host's namespace. An unavailable operation is a readable capability refusal, never a reason for direct SQL or ad hoc Python writes.

Use the available MCP discovery mechanism. No client-specific discovery tool, task mirror, hooks or publisher is assumed.

Discover only the deferred triage tools the selected mode needs.

A tool missing from the server means the server is older than this skill:
tell the user to restart or upgrade it; never imitate the tool by hand.

#### Choose the mode

One mode per request, chosen from the user's words in any language:

| The user says | Mode |
|---|---|
| "record the findings", "open the triage" (after a consolidated review) | **open**, then **page** |
| "build the page", "publish the triage page", "rebuild it" | **page** |
| "Codex filled in the proposals", "redeploy the triage", an agent's answer file | **prefill** |
| the page's generated decision text pasted into the chat, "accept the proposals as final" | **close** |

A word the user merely quotes or mentions is not a command. When the cycle
is unclear (several open cycles fit), ask which one — one option per cycle
code.

**Addressing.** Every MCP triage write takes the cycle as `cycle_id` (the
global id from `open_triage`) OR `cycle` (its code) plus an explicit
`project` — a code needs the project, it is never read as an id, and the MCP
tools never auto-detect it from the working directory. The CLI resolves a
`<code>` from the working directory unless `--project` is given; `--cycle-id
N` needs no project.

**Inspect first (resume rule).** Every mode starts by reading the cycle:
`export_triage(cycle=<code>, project=<slug>)` (or `cycle_id`). What it shows
decides what is still to do — a mode never repeats a write that already
succeeded:

- No such cycle → only **open** may create it.
- An open cycle without cards (a record that failed) → reuse it: record the
  findings into it; never open a second cycle for the same review.
- An open cycle WITH cards → never record them again (a re-recorded card is a
  NEW finding, a duplicate).
- A closed cycle (`closed` is not null) → never decide, accept or close it
  again; only the page build, the publication and the closure note are
  retried. Report it as "ledger closed; publication pending" until they are
  done.

#### Mode: open

The coordinator has consolidated the reviews (rubric §3: findings merged by
fingerprint, class derived) and every review of the diff has finished — the
review → triage → fix gate below.

1. `mcp__dct__open_triage(code, topic, created_by, project, scope,
   base_commit, language)` — `code` a short handle (e.g. `rev-877-r2`), unique among
   the project's live cycles; `created_by=<known_actor_identity>` follows
   the shared known-component rule below (true client sufficient; no guessed
   project or UTC time); `scope` what was reviewed (diff range, files);
   `base_commit` the cycle's fixed base commit; `language` the page
   language of the cycle (omit it to take `[triage] language` of `dct.toml`,
   else `en`) — fixed for the cycle's page, rebuilds and accepted-proposal
   prefix. REMEMBER the returned `cycle_id`.
2. **Purpose and use check** before recording (the class is a recommendation
   and the rubric's threat model is an input to it, not a constant): for every
   card say in its context who supplies the trigger input and whether the
   surface lies within the tool's purpose and trust model — an internal tool
   whose inputs the owner's own process writes, or a surface reached only
   through an artefact the owner authors (a private template), is not
   attacker-controlled. A card reachable only outside that model keeps its
   S but gets O ≤ 1, is not `security`, and gets a class override
   (`cls` backlog or note, `clsWhy` naming the model) instead of fix; its
   context keeps the reviewer's original O and type and the reason for the
   change (rubric §3: a changed field keeps its source value visible). A card
   whose invariant was already fixed in this item and that only adds a new
   trigger of an approximation which cannot be completed case by case (a
   hand-written lexer, parser or sanitizer) is recorded as `cls` decide with
   `clsWhy` "class recurrence: structural change or backlog" — never another
   fix round; the summary says so.
3. `mcp__dct__record_findings(findings=<CARDS>, cycle_id=<id>)` — ONE call
   with the whole array (atomic: one invalid finding = nothing written). Each
   finding carries `src` — the reviewer(s) as free display text (`codex`,
   `panel:security + codex`) — AND `reviewers`, the list of canonical
   reviewer tokens (lowercase, `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9:._-]*$`, no duplicates, e.g.
   `["codex", "panel:security"]`). The coordinator knows who reported what:
   always pass `reviewers`; never derive them by guessing from `src`.
4. The ack's `recorded[]` lists `{seq, finding_id, first_seen_id}`: every
   finding with a non-null `first_seen_id` is a RECURRING fingerprint —
   name it in the summary (K-n and the finding it recurs from).
5. Continue with **page** in the same turn.

#### Mode: page

1. The output path: when the project has `.context/artifacts/`, use
   `.context/artifacts/triage-<safe code>/<safe code>.html`; otherwise the
   session scratchpad, `<scratchpad>/triage-<safe code>/<safe code>.html`.
   `<safe code>` is the cycle code with every character outside
   `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` replaced by `-`. Create the directory first (`mkdir -p`)
   — the CLI refuses a missing parent directory. One page per directory: the
   build keeps its companion files (`cards.json`, `plain.json`) beside it.
2. Build from the ledger:
   `dct triage page <code> --project <slug> --out <path>` (dct builds from
   the template it ships, in the cycle's language, unless `--template
   <path>` or `[triage] template` in `dct.toml` names another; a template
   written before dct shipped its own is refused with the upgrade path —
   pass it on to the user). The CLI
   is read-only on the database and prints `<out>: <n> cards, closed=<yes|no>,
   suggested=<by>, digest=<hex>` (or `suggested=none`) — the digest of the
   proposals exactly as this build put them on the page. It also writes
   `cards.json` beside the page — the export the page was built from, the
   bytes `dct triage export --json` prints — and prints `<dir>/cards.json:
   cards export, <n> cards`. That file is what a consultant reads (the
   cards, their options, proposals and decisions as recorded), never the
   HTML. A rebuild of THE SAME cycle onto its own path adds
   `--force`; never `--force` onto any other path — the published or closed
   page of another cycle is never overwritten.
2a. **The plain-language layer** (section below), when the template reads
   it: write the cycle's plain file and add `--plain <the cycle's plain
   file>` to the build — it validates the file against the cycle's cards,
   copies it as `plain.json` beside the page and prints one more line
   `<dir>/plain.json: plain layer, <n> cards` — then publish the two
   together.
3. When the host refuses the CLI call, give the exact `dct triage page` command to run and continue only from its actual output.
4. Publish only through a publishing/artifact capability actually available and authorized on this host. Use the same local path and destination for a republish when the publisher supports a stable URL; do not claim URL stability without that capability. Descriptions use the conversation language, including their first word, and say the page collects the owner's answers. The page's storage key comes from the cycle id, preserving viewer drafts on a rebuild. With the plain-language layer, publish `plain.json` beside the page as a supporting file on every publish (open, prefill, closed) when the publisher supports supporting files; otherwise report the layer as not published.
5. After the FIRST successful publish, call `update_triage(artifact_url=<actual url>, cycle_id=<id>)` for an open cycle. Do not store a local path as a published URL.
6. If publication is unavailable, return the local artifact and exact next action/command. Report publication pending; a generic MCP connection does not establish a publisher. For proposals record that local build's digest with its exact artifact; acceptance still needs the exact digest of the artifact the owner actually saw. Never invent a published page or require Claude login.

7. The chat carries the status, the link and the count per class
   (`mcp__dct__list_findings(project=<slug>, cycle_id=<id>, limit=0)`, column
   `class`) — never a second set of cards.

#### The plain-language layer

A page template may carry a plain-language layer: the page fetches a file
`plain.json` published beside it and shows, per card, the same finding in
plain words, with a toggle between the plain and the full text. When the
template reads it (its header comment describes the slot), every publish of
the page (open, prefill, closed) carries it:

- **Shape:** `{by, date, cards: {"K-n": {title, problem | was + fix, opts:
  {a: …}, codex, amends}}}` — `by` who wrote the texts
  (`<known_actor_identity>`), `date` the day; per card `title`, then
  `problem` for a card the owner decides, or `was` + `fix` for a card whose
  fix is already applied; `opts` the variants in short, keyed by the card's
  own option letters; `codex` one line summarising each agent proposal;
  `amends` the closed decision a choice would change. Every field is
  optional; a card the file does not name keeps its full text.
- **Content:** two to four plain sentences per card in the language of the
  conversation; numbers, step names and values kept; rubric vocabulary
  (field scores, class names) and decision ids left out.
- **Keys:** only the K-n of this cycle's cards, in `opts` only that card's
  own option letters, only the fields above. `--plain` refuses anything else
  (naming it) and then writes nothing, the page included — fix the file,
  never the page.
- **Place:** the file lives with the cycle's records, e.g.
  `.context/review-<item>/plain-<safe code>.json` (without `.context/`, the
  page's directory). Every build of the page passes it with `--plain`, which
  copies it as `plain.json` into the page's directory, beside the page; a
  `plain.json` already there is replaced only with `--force`, like the page.
  **page** writes the file; **prefill** updates its `codex` lines; **close**
  keeps it, refreshed where a decision changed what a text says.
- **A reading aid, never a decision.** The layer changes no card, no state,
  no proposal and no generated decision text; the ledger stays the source,
  and the proposals' digest does not depend on it (a rebuild leaves it
  unchanged). A changed text means an edited JSON file and a republish; the
  page file is still never hand-edited.
- A template without the slot ignores the file: skip the layer, nothing else
  changes.

#### Mode: prefill

An agent (Codex, a consultant) proposed answers for an OPEN cycle. Its
input is the `cards.json` beside the page (written by every build, see
**page**), never the page's HTML.

1. Read its proposals: a file it left or its answer in the chat, in the
   page's SUGGESTED shape `{by, date, answers: {"K-n": {dec, opt, note}}}`
   (an older flat map `{"K-n": {dec, opt, note}}` is the `answers` alone). An
   agent that edited a page file instead: read its `SUGGESTED` constant from
   that file and NEVER publish the edited file — it is rebuilt from the
   ledger below.
   The agent reads the cards from the `cards.json` beside the page, never from the page's HTML. Use the actual available transport: an agent with permitted DCT MCP writes `suggest_findings` directly, then the coordinator verifies the stored proposals and skips duplicate writes. An agent without permitted MCP leaves `suggested.json` in the SUGGESTED shape for the coordinator to record with `by` = the actual proposer. Background/noninteractive execution alone neither proves nor disproves MCP availability. Never require Claude login or pretend an unavailable tool was called; inspect actual authorization/capability. The ledger records the proposer rather than the file transporter.
2. `mcp__dct__suggest_findings(by=<SUGGESTED.by>,
   suggestions=<SUGGESTED.answers>, cycle_id=<id>)` — for a proposal-input
   envelope, only the intended new
   proposals, keyed by `K-n`, each containing `dec`, `opt`, `note`; never the
   whole `{by, date, answers}` envelope. An export also carries
   `suggested.answers[K-n].by`, the proposer of that individual card; the
   top-level `suggested.by` is only the latest proposer. Both are export
   metadata, not proposal-input keys or owner identity. When reusing exported
   answers, explicitly project the selected cards to `dec`, `opt`, `note` and
   name the actual proposer of this batch in `by`; never replay all mixed-author
   answers under the latest proposer. Untouched cards retain their own
   attribution. Proposals never touch a decision.
3. Rebuild onto the same path (`dct triage page <code> --project <slug>
   --out <path> --force`, plus `--plain` with its `codex` lines updated when
   the page carries the plain-language layer above) and republish to the
   same URL, with its `plain.json`, and a description saying, in the language of the conversation, that the page is open and
   carries proposals by <by>, not decisions ("Open — proposals by <by>, not
   decisions"). **Record the digest** the build printed (`digest=<hex>`):
   it identifies the proposals the owner sees on the published page. Name
   it in the report (`SUGGESTED.digest <hex>`) so a later session finds it;
   the published page also carries it in its `SUGGESTED` constant. A later
   rebuild that changes the proposals publishes a new digest — only the
   digest of the page actually published counts.
4. Optional check: render the page headless, or `node --check` its script.
5. Report the link, how many cards got a proposal, every proposal whose
   variant differs from the card's recommendation, and that the owner's
   answers still come back as the page's generated text pasted into the chat
   (or his explicit acceptance of the proposals).

#### Mode: close

1. **The owner pasted the decision text** →
   `mcp__dct__decide_findings_from_text(text=<the pasted text, verbatim>,
   decided_by="owner", decision_source="chat <YYYY-MM-DD>", cycle_id=<id>)`.
   The text is parsed before anything is written; a parse error (it names
   the line number and the key) writes nothing — report it verbatim and ask
   the owner for the corrected line; never repair his text yourself. A card
   the page left without a decision ("— (no decision)", "— (brak
   decyzji)") and with no note is NOT addressed: it keeps
   its stored state and comes back in the ack's `skipped` — name every
   skipped K-n in the report (they still need the owner's answer). A
   starting-point line ("Starting point:", "Punkt wyjścia:") in the text is
   stored with the decisions as their
   text origin: it shows the form was seeded from proposals, not who wrote
   each note.
2. **The owner accepts the proposals as final** →
   `mcp__dct__accept_suggestions(decided_by="owner",
   decision_source="chat <YYYY-MM-DD>", expected_by=<the SUGGESTED.by of the
   page he saw>, expected_digest=<the digest recorded when that page was
   built and published>, cycle_id=<id>)`. The digest is the one saved in
   **prefill** (the `digest=` line of the `dct triage page` build that was
   published, or the `SUGGESTED.digest` of that local file exactly as
   published in this session) — NEVER a fresh one from `export_triage` or a
   new build, and never a read of the page's current URL as the only proof:
   both can carry proposals he has not seen. No saved digest → do not
   accept: rebuild, republish and let him look again. It refuses when a proposal's
   author differs from `expected_by` or the digest differs (cards or
   proposals changed after he saw them, even by the same author — rebuild,
   republish, record the new digest and let him look again) and when an
   addressed finding already carries a decision; `overwrite=true` only when
   the owner said that his proposals replace earlier decisions. Each
   accepted note is prefixed with its author's name, so a consultant's
   proposal is never presented as the owner's words. `without_suggestion`
   lists the cards it left untouched —
   they need the owner's own text. When he accepts the proposals AND changes
   some cards, accept first, then decide his text: his text wins.
   CLI twins, for a host without the MCP tools (CLI texts are English; the
   parser reads the page's own labels): `dct triage decide <code> --project
   <slug> --from-text <file> --decided-by owner --source "chat <YYYY-MM-DD>"`
   (`--from-text -` reads stdin), `dct triage accept <code> --project <slug>
   --decided-by owner --source "chat <YYYY-MM-DD>" --expected-by <by>
   --expected-digest <the saved digest>`, and
   for step 4 `dct triage close <code> --project <slug> --source "chat
   <YYYY-MM-DD>" --note "<paragraph>"` (`--note` repeatable).
3. **Partial answers.** Only the addressed cards change; the ack's
   `undecided` is the real state after the write. While it is not empty, do
   not close: report the outstanding K-n (the skipped ones included) and
   that the next paste continues (an open page does not show partial
   decisions — they live in the ledger).
4. **Close.** Close only after a real owner step in this mode — his pasted
   text recorded or his acceptance recorded — AND when `undecided` is empty.
   Never close on an agent's proposals alone, and never close a cycle no
   owner answer reached. A `discuss` decision counts as decided for the
   ledger, but the card stays open in substance: the report names it as
   still to be discussed. A closed triage records decisions; it does not
   mean any fix is done.
   `mcp__dct__close_triage(source="chat <YYYY-MM-DD>", notes=[…],
   cycle_id=<id>)` — the notes say what was executed, what the answers do
   NOT approve (a commit, a push, a release) and, after an acceptance, the
   owner's words of acceptance quoted verbatim plus one sentence that the
   per-card notes are the accepted proposal text, not his words. When the
   pasted text carried a starting-point line, it is stored with the decision
   and comes back as `CLOSED.answers[K-n].origin`; a note may quote it too.
   `CLOSED.answers[K-n]` includes this `origin` only when the decision came
   from a prefilled paste; later decisions without that origin reset it.
5. Rebuild onto the same path with `--force` (plus `--plain` when the page
   carries the plain-language layer above) and republish to the same URL,
   with its `plain.json`, and a description starting with the word "Closed" and the date, in the
   language of the conversation ("Closed <YYYY-MM-DD>" in English,
   "Zamknięty <YYYY-MM-DD>" in Polish).
6. **Backlog → dct.** `mcp__dct__list_findings(project=<slug>,
   cycle_id=<the closing cycle's id>, decision="backlog", limit=0)` — only
   THIS cycle's backlog (never the project's whole backlog: earlier cycles
   were handled at their own close), and of those only the findings whose
   `item_id` is still empty (an already linked one is skipped).
   When there are any, ONE decision interaction: "Create dct items for the
   backlog findings of <code>?" with the options "Promote to dct"
   (recommended) — its preview: the screen, one line per finding (`K-n ·
   title`, under 60 characters) — and "Not now". On "Promote to dct":
   `mcp__dct__promote_finding_to_item(finding_id=<id>, project=<slug>)` per
   finding. Neither deciding nor closing creates an item by itself; note and
   reject never create one.
7. **Closure note.** When the review belongs to a tracked item (the item the
   reviewed work was done for), `mcp__dct__add_note(item_id, note="Triage
   <code> closed <YYYY-MM-DD>: <n> fix, <n> verify, <n> backlog, <n> reject,
   <n> note, <n> discuss — <page url>")`. No item known → say so; never pick
   one by guess.
8. **Report**: the link; which decisions approve fixes (each fix / verify K-n
   with its variant); for every open fix / verify finding one explicit
   follow-up sentence — who does what next (the fix to implement, or the
   check to run and its reopen condition per the rubric; an unreproduced
   verify goes to dct tagged `unreproduced`), since closing the triage
   finished none of them; every `discuss` card as still open; the skipped
   cards, if any; the items promoted; and, in plain words, that commit, push
   and release are NOT approved by these answers.

#### Rules

- **Language.** A quoted question, option, screen or report fixes what it
  says, not its wording: write it in the language of the conversation. Keep
  unchanged: identifiers, commands, paths, file contents, commit messages,
  changelog entries, short titles and anything shown verbatim.
The common consent boundary is the exact readable proposal before the user's explicit response. A selected default, timeout, silence, unattended run, old handoff or generated proposal is never approval. Changed scope requires a fresh concrete preview; reuse unchanged explicit consent already given. A report is not a consent request. Keep every proposal word visible before acceptance; hidden thinking, truncated content and a reference to an unavailable screen do not suffice.

Use the current host's eligible consent UI when it exposes complete previews; otherwise show the full decision material in visible text and ask for the explicit reply. Workflow references to dialog previews/Details pages mean the same complete readable content, translated to the current host's supported presentation. Never depend on hidden thinking, omitted pages or a Plan-only/optional-question-only permission tool.
- **Consent.** Decisions come only from the owner's own text. An agent's
  proposals never become decisions without the owner's acceptance. Note and
  reject never create items. `decided_by` / `decision_source` are an audit
  record, never filled for a decision the owner did not make.
- **The review → triage → fix gate.** A review stays read-only; the findings
  are recorded only after every parallel review of the diff has finished; no
  fix starts before the owner's answers approve it — and those answers never
  approve a commit, a push or a release.
- **The page is derived, never edited.** Every page version comes from
  `export_triage` through `dct triage page`; never rebuild a page from
  anything else, never hand-edit its constants, never publish a file another
  agent edited. A published or closed page file is overwritten only by a
  rebuild of its own cycle from the ledger (`--force` onto its own path).
- **Resume, never repeat.** Inspect the cycle first (above). A failed step is
  retried from the ledger's state: a closed cycle is never decided or closed
  again, and an open cycle with cards is never recorded again.
- Errors from a triage tool are reported verbatim; nothing is retried blindly
  and nothing is "fixed" around a refusal.


Use truthful actor identity in `created_by` and `consumed_by`. Only the true client is mandatory. Model, session identifier and session link are included only when supplied by the host; never invent them.

A project suffix is included only from a prior successful DCT response or an explicit user-supplied slug, never a directory, worktree or task-title guess. UTC is included only from an actual provided clock, known host time context or a time tool; no approximate time. Otherwise omit unknown components entirely, including project and time: never fill them with `unknown`, `?`, `0000` or guessed values. Server-created `created_at` / `consumed_at` timestamps remain separate ledger facts.

Use `<known_actor_identity>` in calls. A client-only identity such as `Codex` or `Claude Code` is sufficient when nothing else is known. Full-format example, ONLY when all components are known: `<true client>[-<host-supplied model>] @ <verified project slug> <actual UTC time>`. The same known-component rule applies to creation and consumption.

No mandatory extra lookup or preflight is added to AUTO pickup. Preserve its one-call path; do not obtain a slug by a guessed directory mapping, call a writer to bypass a read-only schema refusal, or require a clock lookup merely to fill an optional component. A status question remains a pure read with no `consumed_by` required.

Identify the actual assistant client. Capability and identity information must come from the running host.

The complete behavior above is generated, not separately authored. Change `dct/skill_sources` and regenerate every target. Missing CLI effect capability is a refusal with its concrete remedy, never a reason to emulate releases through raw ledger writes.
